authors: Dong-hwi Kim, Chaewon Moon, Hojun Song, Dongbeom Kim, Junyeong Jang, Aro Kim, Gahyeon Kim, Heejung Choi, Jehee Kim, Gianella Cravioto, Sohyun Lee, Gyeongjin Choi, EunHye Jeong, Soo Ye Kim, Jaehyup Lee, Sang-hyo Park
bullets: Lossy compression disrupts cross-view geometry, harming feature matching, correspondence, camera estimation, and novel-view synthesis.
CompMVR jointly restores compressed views while preserving geometric consistency across views.
The framework combines learned compression priors with cross-view correspondence rather than restoring images independently.
Compressed datasets enable evaluation across diverse datasets, codecs, and compression levels.
Experiments report improved restoration quality and downstream performance in novel-view synthesis, camera pose estimation, and view matching.
papers.selection_reason: Compression-aware multi-view restoration with cross-view consistency directly supports 3D reconstruction and novel-view synthesis.
papers.title: CompMVR: Compression-Aware Multi-View Restoration Using Diffusion Models for Geometrically Consistent 3D Reconstruction
papers.tldr: CompMVR uses diffusion-based, cross-view-aware restoration to reduce compression-induced inconsistencies and improve multi-view 3D reconstruction.

papers.abstract: Generating editable 3D urban scenes from a single image requires detailed building assets with a coherent spatial arrangement. Occlusion and perspective ambiguity make it difficult to infer complete building geometry together with consistent relative scales and positions. We present CityLift, a framework that generates individual textured building meshes from an urban image by coupling scene-level spatial modeling with building-level synthesis. CityLift first learns building shape and placement jointly through coupled scene and instance streams, producing coarse sparse structures in a common coordinate system. We then introduce generative spatial inheritance, which maps each building's coarse occupancy and scene-conditioned 3D feature field into a local volume to guide a flow model that generates finer structure. The same coordinate mapping places the generated meshes back into the scene, preserving their spatial relationship to the scaffold. To address the scarcity of urban data pairing scene images with individual 3D buildings, we construct CityLift-5K, comprising 4,997 synthetic scenes with instance masks, building meshes, and placement annotations. Experiments on CityLift-5K and scene blocks from UrbanScene3D and InstanceBuilding demonstrate improved building geometry and scene composition. The project page is available at https://ranhaogong.github.io/CityLift/.
authors: Haoran Gong, Jie Feng, Chenxu Wang
bullets: Addresses occlusion and perspective ambiguity in reconstructing complete buildings with consistent scales and positions.
Uses coupled scene- and instance-level streams to produce coarse building shapes and placements in a shared coordinate system.
Introduces generative spatial inheritance to guide flow-based refinement of detailed textured building meshes.
Builds CityLift-5K, a dataset of 4,997 synthetic scenes with masks, meshes, and placement annotations.
Experiments on CityLift-5K and UrbanScene3D scene blocks show improved building geometry and scene composition.
papers.selection_reason: Presents a framework for compositional 3D urban scene generation from a single image, addressing the scarcity of paired data. This contributes to 3D scene understanding and generation.
papers.title: CityLift: Compositional 3D Urban Generation from a Single Image
papers.tldr: CityLift generates editable 3D urban scenes from a single image by jointly modeling building geometry and spatial arrangement.

papers.abstract: We introduce SemGeo-Gen, an unsupervised method for generating approximate cross-instance semantic-geometric supervision from weakly aligned 3D object collections. Our goal is not to recover exact point-level correspondences, which are often ambiguous across different instances and would require expensive, impractical manual supervision at scale. Instead, we automatically produce approximate correspondences that are semantically meaningful, geometrically consistent, and diverse enough to train modern correspondence models. Given only coarse category-level rotation alignment, SemGeo-Gen lifts multi-view DINOv2 features to 3D, aligns object instances using continuous piecewise-affine registration, and prunes candidate matches using semantic consistency. The resulting 3D correspondences can be projected into rendered views, yielding scalable 3D-3D, 3D-2D, and 2D-2D supervision without manual annotation. We validate the generated correspondences against sparse human annotations from KeypointNet, obtaining 93% PCK@0.10 and 97% PCK@0.15. More importantly, we show that using the generated correspondences for synthetic pretraining improves recent state-of-the-art semantic correspondence models on SPair-71k after fine-tuning on real data, with gains of up to 5 PCK@0.10 points. Together, these results indicate that approximate semantic-geometric supervision generated from 3D assets can improve real-image correspondence learning and serve as a scalable alternative to costly manual annotation. Project page: https://bgu-cs-vil.github.io/SemGeo-Gen/.
authors: Roy Amoyal, Shira Ifergane, Oren Freifeld
bullets: Addresses the ambiguity and cost of exact point-level correspondence annotation across object instances.
Lifts multi-view DINOv2 features into 3D, aligns instances with continuous piecewise-affine registration, and filters matches by semantic consistency.
Projects the generated 3D matches into rendered views to produce 3D-3D, 3D-2D, and 2D-2D supervision.
Generated correspondences achieve 93% PCK@0.10 and 97% PCK@0.15 against sparse KeypointNet annotations.
Synthetic pretraining with this supervision improves SPair-71k correspondence models by up to 5 PCK@0.10 points after real-data fine-tuning.
papers.selection_reason: Unsupervised generation of semantic-geometric 3D correspondences for pretraining is directly relevant to 3D vision and scalable supervision.
papers.title: SemGeo-Gen: Unsupervised Generation of Approximate Cross-Instance Semantic-Geometric Correspondences
papers.tldr: SemGeo-Gen automatically creates scalable, approximate 2D/3D semantic-geometric correspondences from weakly aligned 3D objects, improving correspondence learning without manual annotation.

papers.abstract: Recent advances in 3D semantic segmentation have significantly improved scene understanding in autonomous driving. However, existing methods are typically developed under a closed-set assumption and evaluated under standard driving conditions, where all categories are known in advance. In real-world driving, autonomous vehicles inevitably encounter previously unseen objects, making closed-set perception insufficient for safe deployment. To address this challenge, we introduce DriveOSS, which, to the best of our knowledge, is the first real-world multimodal dataset and benchmark specifically designed for 3D anomaly segmentation and open-set semantic segmentation. It contains 12,661 synchronized and annotated frames captured using six surround-view RGB cameras, a 128-beam LiDAR, and a GPS/IMU unit. The dataset comprises 52 real-world driving scenes collected under clear, nighttime, cloudy, rainy, and snowy conditions and is organized into ID (in-distribution) and OOD (out-of-distribution) subsets. The ID scenes contain only known classes and are used for training, whereas the OOD scenes additionally contain unknown objects annotated as the outlier class and are used for validation and testing. Extensive experiments show that unseen objects remain a major challenge for current 3D perception systems. The dataset, benchmark protocols, and code are available at https://github.com/chrisyan/DriveOSS.
authors: Zhiran Yan, Savankumar Bhanderi, Sourabh Lolge, Rui Song, Girdharbhai Paneliya, Shiva Agrawal, Gordon Elger
bullets: Addresses the safety gap caused by closed-set 3D perception systems that cannot recognize previously unseen objects.
Provides 12,661 synchronized, annotated frames from six RGB cameras, 128-beam LiDAR, and GPS/IMU sensors.
Covers 52 driving scenes across clear, nighttime, cloudy, rainy, and snowy conditions.
Separates known-class ID training scenes from OOD validation and test scenes containing annotated unknown objects.
Experiments show that unseen objects remain a major challenge for current 3D perception systems; data, protocols, and code are publicly available.
papers.selection_reason: Introduces a real-world dataset and benchmark for 3D anomaly segmentation and open-set semantic segmentation in autonomous driving. This contributes to 3D perception capabilities required for safe navigation.
papers.title: DriveOSS: Dataset and Benchmark for 3D Anomaly Segmentation and Open-set Semantic Segmentation in Autonomous Driving
papers.tldr: DriveOSS introduces a real-world multimodal benchmark for evaluating 3D anomaly segmentation and open-set semantic segmentation in autonomous driving.

papers.abstract: Real-time decoding of omnidirectional images is essential for immersive virtual reality (VR) experiences. Compared with conventional transform-based learned image compression (LIC), overfitted codecs offer lower decoding complexity by representing each image with a lightweight implicit neural representation (INR). However, existing approaches typically operate on the equirectangular projection (ERP), which introduces nonuniform spherical sampling and spatial distortion, leading to redundant sampling near the poles and latitude-dependent receptive fields. To address these limitations, we propose a spherical overfitted codec based on a multi-scale Hierarchical Equal Area isoLatitude Pixelization (HEALPix) representation, which enables equal-area sampling and efficient hierarchical modeling of spherical signals. Building on this representation, we develop a Spherical Inter-Scale Conditional entropy model that exploits spatial dependencies and cross-scale correlations among HEALPix latents to improve coding efficiency. We further introduce a Multi-Ring Spherical Convolution that aggregates neighboring pixels over a nearly uniform spherical receptive field across latitudes. Experiments on a public omnidirectional image dataset demonstrate BD-rate reductions of 16.3%, 26.5%, and 19.5% over VVC in terms of V-PSNR, V-MS-SSIM, and V-LPIPS, respectively. Our method also achieves a 13.1% BD-rate reduction over ERP-based Cool-Chic 5.0 in terms of V-PSNR, while providing 2.6-3.6x faster decoding than the evaluated learned autoencoder codecs.
authors: Yulong Cheng, Youneng Bao, Junfeng Zhou, Mu Li, Jie Wen
bullets: Addresses ERP distortion and redundant polar sampling in omnidirectional image compression.
Uses multi-scale HEALPix representation with a spherical inter-scale conditional entropy model.
Introduces multi-ring spherical convolution for nearly uniform receptive fields across latitudes.
Reduces BD-rate versus VVC by 16.3% (V-PSNR), 26.5% (V-MS-SSIM), and 19.5% (V-LPIPS).
Achieves 13.1% lower BD-rate than ERP-based Cool-Chic 5.0 in V-PSNR and 2.6–3.6× faster decoding than evaluated learned autoencoders.
papers.selection_reason: Proposes an implicit neural compression scheme for omnidirectional images using HEALPix representation. This contributes to 3D perception and representation techniques, specifically for spherical geometry.
papers.title: HEALPix-Based Implicit Neural Compression of Omnidirectional Images
papers.tldr: A HEALPix-based implicit neural codec improves omnidirectional image compression efficiency and decoding speed by modeling spherical signals with uniform sampling and cross-scale dependencies.

papers.abstract: Developing multiple instance learning pipelines for the classification of whole-slide images involves many interdependent design decisions and expertise in both pathology and machine learning. We present AutoMIL, an open-source framework that applies principles from the field of automated machine learning to tackle this task by automating integral pipeline steps, such as preprocessing, training and evaluation. In a benchmark evaluation with default settings, AutoMIL reached ROC-AUC scores of 0.94 on UBC-OCEAN, 0.99 on PCam and 0.93-0.96 on a TCGA-NSCLC subset, comparable to specialised pipelines in related work. Ensembling mainly improved performance on imbalanced data, showing that an automated pipeline must adapt to dataset characteristics. AutoMIL thus provides an accessible baseline for whole-slide image classification without manual pipeline configuration.
authors: Jonas Waibel, Frank Kramer, Dominik M\"uller
bullets: Addresses the expertise and configuration burden of designing whole-slide image classification pipelines.
Automates preprocessing, training, and evaluation using automated machine learning principles.
Achieves ROC-AUC scores of 0.94 on UBC-OCEAN, 0.99 on PCam, and 0.93–0.96 on a TCGA-NSCLC subset.
Ensembling primarily benefits imbalanced datasets, highlighting the need to adapt automation to dataset characteristics.
Provides an open-source baseline without manual pipeline configuration.
papers.selection_reason: Applies automated machine learning to whole-slide image classification, fitting the 3D Vision category (specifically 3D Foundation Models).
papers.title: AutoMIL: Automated Multiple Instance Learning for Whole-Slide Image Classification
papers.tldr: AutoMIL automates key multiple instance learning pipeline decisions for whole-slide image classification, providing an accessible baseline with competitive benchmark performance.

papers.abstract: 3D MLLMs recognize objects via pattern matching, which fails when geometrically similar objects require functional reasoning to disambiguate (e.g., dresser vs. wardrobe). Our per-sample Geometric Confusion Score (GCS) exposes this failure: baseline accuracy is 33.7% on ModelNet40's most ambiguous 20% versus 84.0% on its least ambiguous 20%. We identify a function-as-annotation pattern, in which functional language decorates a known identity instead of supporting inference, and hypothesize that reversing this information flow should concentrate improvements on the most ambiguous samples. PFIR (Part-level Functional Inference for Recognition) reverses that flow. Built on PartNeXt part segmentation, its data pipeline produces 507K QA pairs with functional CoTs (geometry $\to$ function $\to$ identity), and its progressive curriculum culminates in dual-objective GRPO: strict functional reasoning and descriptive grounding for Objaverse's diverse distribution. The two RL objectives yield nearly orthogonal task vectors ($\cos = 0.056$), enabling composition via Task Arithmetic. Under a strict dual OOD protocol (Objaverse $\to$ ModelNet40; XYZRGB $\to$ XYZ-only), PFIR raises zero-shot accuracy from 60.5% to 66.7%, with gains concentrated $2.6\times$ more on geometrically ambiguous samples---supporting part-level functional reasoning as an effective route to more generalizable 3D recognition. Code: https://github.com/this233/pfir-3d.
authors: Weihong Li, Hao Jiang, Yaohua Zha, Tao Dai, Shu-Tao Xia
bullets: Pattern-matching 3D MLLMs struggle to distinguish geometrically similar objects, with accuracy dropping sharply on highly ambiguous samples.
The method reverses the usual information flow: geometry → function → identity, using part-level segmentation and functional chain-of-thought supervision.
PFIR trains on 507K functional QA pairs with a progressive curriculum and combines functional reasoning with descriptive grounding through dual-objective GRPO.
Under Objaverse→ModelNet40 and XYZRGB→XYZ-only zero-shot evaluation, accuracy improves from 60.5% to 66.7%.
Improvements are concentrated 2.6× more on geometrically ambiguous samples, supporting part-level functional reasoning for recognition.
papers.selection_reason: Part-level functional reasoning in 3D MLLMs to improve generalizable 3D recognition; relevant to 3D foundation models and spatial intelligence.
papers.title: Beyond Pattern Matching in 3D MLLMs: Part-Level Functional Reasoning for Generalizable Recognition
papers.tldr: PFIR improves generalizable 3D object recognition by inferring function from parts before identifying the object, especially in geometrically ambiguous cases.

papers.abstract: Single-image 3D scene construction is a fundamental problem in 3D vision. Recent methods such as SAM-3Dfy enable end-to-end reconstruction of 3D assets and their scene layouts, but still struggle with fine-grained scene geometry and asset quality. Meanwhile, specialized 3D object generators provide detailed object geometry, while 3D foundation models offer strong and generalizable spatial understanding. We propose Easy-3Dfy, a compositional workflow that decouples object generation from scene layout estimation, allowing specialized models to fully exploit their respective strengths. An RPF-based aligner then bridges these capabilities by establishing geometric correspondence between object-local meshes and partial scene pointmaps, recovering object layout for scene composition. Without requiring complete scene-level supervision, the proposed workflow consistently outperforms SAM-3Dfy across multiple geometric metrics on Scene-Maker and 3D-FUTURE200. Our results demonstrate that explicit geometric composition can effectively combine high-quality object generation with strong spatial understanding, while enabling the workflow to benefit independently from advances in both 3D object generation and foundation models.
authors: Ziang Zhang, Wenyou Yi, Zehan Wang, Jiachen Xu, Xintong Han, Chunchao Guo, Zhou Zhao
bullets: Targets limitations in fine-grained scene geometry and asset quality in existing end-to-end methods such as SAM-3Dfy.
Uses specialized 3D object generators for object geometry and 3D foundation models for spatial understanding.
An RPF-based aligner matches object-local meshes with partial scene pointmaps to recover object layouts.
Requires no complete scene-level supervision and outperforms SAM-3Dfy across multiple geometric metrics on Scene-Maker and 3D-FUTURE200.
Its modular design can independently benefit from advances in object generation and foundation models.
papers.selection_reason: Single-image 3D scene construction via geometric composition, linking 3D object generation with spatial understanding from foundation models.
papers.title: Easy-3Dfy: Object-Level Geometric Composition for Single-Image 3D Scene Construction
papers.tldr: Easy-3Dfy improves single-image 3D scene reconstruction by separately generating detailed objects and estimating their spatial layout, then aligning them geometrically for composition.

papers.abstract: Humans reason about the physical world by flexibly combining different forms of inference as a problem unfolds. Achieving this flexibility is a major open challenge in AI: capabilities often remain separated across specialized models, limiting how they can be composed and jointly adapted to a task. We introduce $\Psi$-0.6, a unified vision-language world model that adaptively composes perception, language, geometry, and simulation within a shared reasoning process we call streams of thought. These streams interleave images, text, and explicit representations of geometry and motion, all of which the model can generate and interpret through a shared token interface. $\Psi$-0.6 surpasses leading open-weight models zero-shot on multi-view spatial reasoning, with further gains from reasoning through geometric intermediates. It also supports counterfactual simulation: generating and interpreting imagined scenes to determine, for example, whether moving an object would obstruct a pathway. Reinforcement learning from task feedback jointly optimizes the selection, generation, and use of intermediate representations, improving visual question-answering accuracy with gains that transfer to unseen benchmarks. $\Psi$-0.6 offers a path toward adaptive physical reasoning -- not only predicting the physical world but also choosing the representations through which to reason.
authors: Khai Loong Aw, Klemen Kotar, Baihan Zhang, Yifan Liu, Lilian Chen, Atlas Kazemian, Rahul Venkatesh, Daniel Yamins
bullets: Interleaves images, text, geometry, and motion representations as composable “streams of thought” through a shared token interface.
Performs zero-shot multi-view spatial reasoning and benefits from explicit geometric intermediate reasoning.
Supports counterfactual simulation, such as predicting whether moving an object would block a path.
Reinforcement learning from task feedback improves intermediate-representation selection and visual question answering, with gains transferring to unseen benchmarks.
The abstract focuses on adaptive physical reasoning; specific limitations and quantitative results are not reported.
papers.selection_reason: Unified vision-language world model with geometric/spatial reasoning and counterfactual simulation directly fits world models, spatial intelligence, and 3D reasoning.
papers.title: $\Psi$-0.6: Adaptive Streams of Thought in a Unified Vision-Language World Model
papers.tldr: Ψ-0.6 is a unified vision-language world model that adaptively combines visual, linguistic, geometric, and simulated reasoning for flexible physical-world inference.

papers.abstract: We present PixGR, an efficient framework that integrates lightweight pixel-space generative modeling into feed-forward 3D Gaussian reconstruction to model scene uncertainty. Context observations are encoded once into a scene latent representation, which conditions generative decoding from noisy target views to produce a shared 3D Gaussian representation. We formulate this process using pixel-space flow matching, enabling end-to-end optimization of 3D reconstruction with direct pixel-space generative supervision through differentiable rendering. This avoids VAE-based latent compression and error propagation inherent in previous two-stage pipelines. To preserve feed-forward efficiency, PixGR caches the scene representation and performs iterative inference using a lightweight DiT decoder. Experiments demonstrate that PixGR outperforms regression-based approaches in challenging sparse-view settings, particularly with widely spaced observations and view extrapolation. Meanwhile, it maintains sub-second inference and remains competitive with substantially heavier pretrained generative models. Our project page is available at https://ranrhuang.github.io/pixgr/.
authors: Ranran Huang, Wenjing Bian, Weixun Luo, Ye Mao, Krystian Mikolajczyk
bullets: Targets sparse-view 3D reconstruction, especially widely spaced observations and view extrapolation.
Encodes context views once into a scene latent that conditions generation from noisy target views.
Uses pixel-space flow matching and differentiable rendering for end-to-end reconstruction supervision.
Avoids VAE-based latent compression and associated error propagation in two-stage pipelines.
Achieves sub-second inference, outperforming regression methods while remaining competitive with heavier generative models.
papers.selection_reason: Pixel-space generative flow matching for feed-forward 3D Gaussian reconstruction; relevant to 3D reconstruction and generative 3D perception.
papers.title: PixGR: Pixel-Space Generative Decoding for Fast Feed-Forward 3D Reconstruction
papers.tldr: PixGR enables fast, uncertainty-aware feed-forward 3D Gaussian reconstruction by combining cached scene representations with lightweight pixel-space generative decoding.

papers.abstract: Generating physically stable 3D structures from visual specifications requires resolving geometric ambiguity while accounting for physical interactions among objects. We present StackGen3D, a framework for generating stable block assemblies conditioned on a given block inventory and three orthographic silhouettes. Our approach consists of two stages. First, we develop a physics-informed graph neural network (PI-GNN) that models support relations between blocks and serves as a fast stability predictor for curating a diverse dataset of stable structures. Second, we train a conditional flow-matching model on this dataset to capture the multimodal distribution of block configurations consistent with the target silhouettes. At inference time, lightweight geometric selection and refinement reduce inter-block penetration without physics simulation. Preliminary experiments show that the PI-GNN generalizes from simple stacks to complex structures substantially better than a parameter-matched multilayer perceptron. For structure generation, Best-of-10 selection improves physical stability from 45.3% to 72.4% while achieving a silhouette IoU of 0.970. These results highlight the potential of combining relational physical reasoning, scalable data curation, and conditional generative modeling for creative 3D assembly. Project website: [https://ripl.github.io/StackGen3D-web/](https://ripl.github.io/StackGen3D-web/)
authors: Xiaopeng Zhang, Luzhe Sun, Yiqing Xu, Matthew R. Walter
bullets: Addresses geometric ambiguity and physical interactions in silhouette-conditioned 3D structure generation.
Uses a physics-informed graph neural network to model block support relations and curate stable training structures.
Trains a conditional flow-matching model to represent multiple valid block configurations.
Applies geometric selection and refinement to reduce inter-block penetration without physics simulation.
Best-of-10 selection reaches 72.4% physical stability with 0.970 silhouette IoU; PI-GNN generalizes better than a parameter-matched MLP.
papers.selection_reason: Generative 3D block-stack assembly from silhouettes with physics-informed stability modeling; fits 3D geometry generation and physical-structure reasoning.
papers.title: StackGen3D: Stable 3D Block Stack Generation from Multiview Silhouettes
papers.tldr: StackGen3D generates physically stable 3D block assemblies from three orthographic silhouettes and a block inventory using physics-aware stability prediction and conditional generative modeling.

papers.abstract: Estimating a camera pose from 3D-2D correspondences - Perspective-n-Point - is one of the most fundamental problems in computer vision. Existing methods either solve a minimal problem or replace the objective with an easier one. Surprisingly, no scalable certifiable solver for the actual Maximum Likelihood Estimation (MLE) exists. We propose PnP*, the first practical solver that guarantees efficient computation and returns a certifiable globally optimal solution. We prove that the underlying convex relaxation is exact under moderate noise, which to our knowledge is the first stability guarantee for any relaxation for the MLE of PnP. Furthermore, we reduce the relaxation by exploiting chordal sparsity pattern and quotient ring reduction such that the relaxation is tractable and scalable. The stability and scalability results are verified numerically, as PnP* returns a provably correct camera pose at over 10 Hz.
authors: Bang-Shien Chen, Caitrin E. Eaton, David M. Rosen
bullets: Addresses the lack of scalable certifiable solvers for the true PnP maximum-likelihood objective.
Uses a convex relaxation with a proof of exactness under moderate noise.
Exploits chordal sparsity and quotient-ring reduction to make the relaxation tractable and scalable.
Numerical experiments verify stability and scalability, with certified solutions reported at over 10 Hz.
papers.selection_reason: Certifiable globally optimal PnP solver with convex relaxation and stability guarantees; relevant to 3D geometry perception, though not learning-based.
papers.title: PnP*: A certifiable solver for Perspective-n-Point
papers.tldr: PnP* is a scalable, certifiable solver for the exact maximum-likelihood Perspective-n-Point problem that can return a provably globally optimal camera pose in real time.

papers.abstract: Generating multiple videos of a dynamic scene from a single reference video requires synthesizing both observed and unobserved content consistently across viewpoints. Existing camera-control methods for video diffusion typically rely on architectural mechanisms, including camera embeddings, cross-view attention, and geometric conditioning. Although effective for static scene content, these approaches often struggle with the fine-grained, dynamic geometry that must remain coherent across views and over time. We synchronize the diffusion process itself by sampling the Gaussian noise prior in a canonical 3D space derived from the source video and rasterizing it into target cameras, rather than sampling independently in each 2D image plane. Our method, SyncVid, lifts a monocular video into a canonical 4D representation, associates noise with scene geometry and unseen space, and rasterizes the resulting structured noise into arbitrary views. Because rendering can introduce local correlations, we further propose a cross-view-consistent whitening procedure that decorrelates neighboring pixels while preserving correspondence across views. The structured noise serves as the diffusion prior for a LoRA-adapted pretrained video diffusion model, requiring no architectural modifications. By enforcing spatiotemporal and cross-view coherence at the source of stochasticity, SyncVid generates synchronized videos and improves both perceptual quality and cross-view consistency in our experiments. Project page: https://qualcomm-ai-research.github.io/SyncVid-Webpage.
authors: Farhad G. Zanjani, Animesh Karnewar, Fatih Porikli, Amirhossein Habibian
bullets: Addresses the challenge of generating temporally and cross-view coherent videos from a single reference video, especially for dynamic geometry.
Lifts the source video into a canonical 4D representation and rasterizes geometry-aware noise into target camera views.
Introduces cross-view-consistent whitening to reduce local correlations while preserving correspondence across views.
Uses the structured noise as the prior for a LoRA-adapted pretrained video diffusion model without architectural modifications.
Experiments report improved perceptual quality and cross-view consistency, though the abstract provides no quantitative results.
papers.selection_reason: World-equivariant diffusion noise for synchronized multi-view video generation; directly advances diffusion-based video generation with cross-view consistency.
papers.title: SyncVid: World-Equivariant Diffusion for Synchronized Video Generation
papers.tldr: SyncVid synchronizes multi-view video generation by coordinating diffusion noise in a canonical 3D space, improving visual quality and cross-view consistency without changing the model architecture.

papers.abstract: Existing 3D talking avatar methods mainly rely on parametric face models including 3DMM or FLAME, whose compact motion representations limit their ability to synthesize extreme expressions and to model accessories such as headwear. We introduce AudioLift, a two-stage framework that uses generated multi-view videos as the intermediate representation for audio-driven avatar generation without parametric face models or per-instance optimization. Our framework combines a synchronized multi-view video generation stage with an inconsistency-robust Gaussian reconstruction stage to recover coherent full-head geometry from a single portrait image. Extensive experiments demonstrate that AudioLift produces 3D talking avatars capable of capturing more extreme facial expressions than existing methods, with improved geometric completeness and strong multi-view consistency across the full $360^\circ$ viewing range.
authors: Zhuoyuan Jiang, Weijie Lyu, Xiaoyuan Wang, Tiancheng Shen, Ming-Hsuan Yang
bullets: Addresses the limited expression range and poor accessory modeling of 3DMM/FLAME-based avatars.
Uses a two-stage pipeline: synchronized multi-view video generation followed by inconsistency-robust Gaussian reconstruction.
Requires neither parametric face models nor per-instance optimization.
Produces more extreme facial expressions, more complete geometry, and strong consistency across 360° views.
Scope: results are reported for audio-driven single-image avatar generation; specific datasets and quantitative results are not given.
papers.selection_reason: 3D talking-avatar generation from a single image via multi-view video synthesis and Gaussian reconstruction; relevant to 3D generation and video-based synthesis.
papers.title: AudioLift: Audio-Driven Single Image to Full-Head Gaussian Avatar via Multi-view Video Generation
papers.tldr: AudioLift creates full-head 3D talking avatars from one portrait and audio by generating synchronized multi-view video, enabling extreme expressions and complete, view-consistent geometry without parametric face models.

papers.abstract: High-quality 3D reconstruction of lunar terrain from sparse rover images is indispensable for autonomous lunar exploration, but remains challenging because viewpoint overlap is insufficient, surface textures are weak, and data volume is limited. We propose MoonGS, the first feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting framework tailored to lunar scenes. Given only two input images, MoonGS predicts pixel-aligned Gaussian primitives in a single forward pass and renders photorealistic novel views without any per-scene optimization. MoonGS (i) adopts an adaptable backbone design that seamlessly integrates advanced vision foundation models to extract robust depth features; (ii) integrates semantic priors in two manners: merging semantic cues with visual features to refine Gaussian parameter estimation, and adopting a semantic ranking loss that regularizes background depth; and (iii) employs an entropy-guided heuristic resampling strategy to augment sparse observations by selecting the most informative distant viewpoints with negligible overhead. Experiments on the LuSNAR benchmark and our synthetic weak-texture MoonBlender dataset show that MoonGS surpasses state-of-the-art feed-forward NeRF/3DGS baselines by +4.9 dB PSNR, +0.29 SSIM, and 40\% lower LPIPS while maintaining sub-second inference. Furthermore, we validate the broad applicability of our framework by demonstrating that it effectively leverages state-of-the-art backbones, including VGGT, to significantly boost performance. Qualitative evaluations on Chang'e mission imagery also show the best visual quality among compared methods, indicating robustness on real lunar data. The source code and dataset are publicly available at https://github.com/InRobots/MoonBlender.
bullets: Addresses sparse-view lunar reconstruction challenges caused by low overlap, weak textures, and limited data.
Predicts pixel-aligned 3D Gaussian primitives in one forward pass, avoiding per-scene optimization.
Uses adaptable vision backbones, semantic feature fusion, semantic ranking loss, and entropy-guided viewpoint resampling.
Outperforms feed-forward NeRF/3DGS baselines on LuSNAR and MoonBlender, with sub-second inference and improved visual quality on Chang'e imagery.
Demonstrates compatibility with advanced backbones such as VGGT.
papers.selection_reason: Feed-forward 3D Gaussian reconstruction of lunar scenes from sparse image pairs directly contributes to 3D vision and 3D scene generation.
papers.title: MoonGS: High-quality Representation of the Lunar Surface via Gaussian Splatting Using Robust Depth Features from Image Pairs
papers.tldr: MoonGS enables fast, high-quality lunar 3D reconstruction from just two rover images by combining robust depth features, semantic priors, and informative-view resampling with feed-forward Gaussian Splatting.

papers.abstract: Quadrotors are increasingly deployed in applications such as agriculture, infrastructure inspection, and maintenance. In each of these applications, the robot must navigate complex scene geometry while remaining strictly collision-free. Unlike in ground domains, even minor collisions for aerial vehicles can result in the loss of the robot. This safety requirement induces a pair of technical challenges. First, the environment must be represented with sufficient fidelity to encode complex structure, even when no ground-truth obstacle data is available. Second, a motion planner must leverage this representation to determine a collision-free path to the goal. This paper proposes a system that addresses these complementary challenges. The proposed method, AirSplan, adopts a normalized variant of 3D Gaussian Splatting that encodes high-fidelity scene geometry. It then applies a novel reachability-based motion planner that leverages the differential flatness of quadrotors to compute continuous-time collision constraints that tightly overapproximate the robot's occupancy. Experiments demonstrate that AirSplan successfully finds a path in 81.2% of challenging test cases, a significant improvement over the nearest baseline method's 51.2%.
bullets: Addresses safe aerial navigation when accurate ground-truth obstacle data is unavailable.
Uses a normalized 3D Gaussian Splatting representation to encode detailed scene geometry.
Introduces a reachability-based planner exploiting quadrotor differential flatness.
Computes continuous-time collision constraints that tightly overapproximate vehicle occupancy.
Finds paths in 81.2% of challenging test cases, compared with 51.2% for the nearest baseline.
papers.selection_reason: Risk-aware quadrotor motion planning using a normalized 3D Gaussian Splatting scene representation; relevant to robot navigation and 3D scene modeling.
papers.title: AirSplan: Risk-Aware Motion Planning for Quadrotors in Cluttered 3D Gaussian Splats
papers.tldr: AirSplan combines high-fidelity 3D Gaussian Splatting with risk-aware reachability planning to find collision-free quadrotor paths in cluttered environments.

papers.abstract: 3D semantic occupancy prediction is crucial for autonomous driving, but camera-based methods degrade in low-light conditions and LiDAR-based methods are sensitive to adverse weather. 4D radar is more robust, yet its sparsity and the high cost of radar tensor processing limit its use. We propose Radar Geometric-Semantic Occupancy Prediction (RadarGSOcc), an efficient framework that directly processes 4D radar tensors by separately extracting geometric and semantic features, including Doppler information, with a deformable attention-based geometric refinement module as its key component. We also introduce the K-Radar 3DSemOcc benchmark, the first large-scale benchmark for 3D semantic occupancy prediction using 4D radar tensors, built on the K-Radar dataset with refined LiDAR-based annotations. RadarGSOcc predicts 15 classes within a 51.2m range and achieves 38.2% IoU, 7.6% mIoU, and 25.5% weighted mIoU, outperforming RadarOcc by 17% relative (25.5 vs. 21.9) in weighted mIoU while using fewer parameters and lower computation. It substantially improves truck prediction while trading off car accuracy, outperforms camera-based approaches, and narrows the gap with LiDAR-based methods. To assess robustness without per-frame ground truth in adverse weather, we further propose a novel proxy metric, Environment-Based KL Divergence (EBKL), under which 4D radar proves a reliable and efficient modality for 3D semantic occupancy prediction. The dataset and code will be publicly available.
bullets: Addresses camera degradation in low light and LiDAR sensitivity to adverse weather, while tackling 4D radar sparsity and processing cost.
Separately extracts geometric and semantic features, including Doppler information, with deformable-attention geometric refinement.
Introduces K-Radar 3DSemOcc, a large-scale 4D-radar semantic occupancy benchmark with refined LiDAR annotations.
Predicts 15 classes within 51.2 m, reaching 38.2% IoU, 7.6% mIoU, and 25.5% weighted mIoU.
Outperforms RadarOcc in weighted mIoU with fewer parameters and lower computation; improves truck prediction but trades off car accuracy.
papers.selection_reason: 3D semantic occupancy prediction from 4D radar with geometric-semantic features is directly relevant to 3D scene perception.
papers.title: RadarGSOcc: Doppler-Aware 3D Semantic Occupancy Prediction Using 4D Radar Tensor with Geometric-Semantic Feature Extraction
papers.tldr: RadarGSOcc efficiently uses Doppler-aware 4D radar tensors for robust 3D semantic occupancy prediction, achieving 25.5% weighted mIoU while reducing computation and parameters.

papers.abstract: Controllable 3D part generation is pivotal for digital asset creation, yet existing methods lack the flexibility to accommodate diverse user workflows requiring varying levels of control. In this paper, we introduce FlexPart, a unified image-to-3D part generation framework that supports variable-granularity geometric conditions within a single model. By seamlessly integrating heterogeneous inputs, ranging from sparse points to dense bounding boxes and masks, via gated adaptive modulation, FlexPart unlocks a powerful cross-modal synergy. We also propose an asymmetric geometric guidance mechanism that leverages strong spatial priors to align representations across granularities, improving geometric consistency and facilitating inter-task synergy. Under mask conditioning on PartVerseXL, FlexPart reduces Part CD by 16.6% relative to TripoSG + SAM3D and by 10.5% relative to OmniPart, while maintaining competitive whole-mesh quality. The code can be found at https://github.com/Gucci233/FlexPart
authors: Qiwen Gu, Xin Zhou, Xiwu Chen, Zhongyang Zhu, Zhuo Zhang, Junqiao Zhao
bullets: Addresses the need for flexible, variable-granularity control in 3D part generation.
Integrates heterogeneous geometric inputs using gated adaptive modulation.
Uses asymmetric geometric guidance to align representations across granularities and promote cross-task synergy.
On PartVerseXL with mask conditioning, reduces Part CD by 16.6% versus TripoSG + SAM3D and 10.5% versus OmniPart.
Maintains competitive whole-mesh quality.
papers.selection_reason: Unified image-to-3D part generation directly fits 3D vision.
papers.title: A Unified Framework for Image-to-3D Part Generation via Variable Granularity
papers.tldr: FlexPart is a unified image-to-3D part generation model that supports controls from sparse points to dense boxes and masks while improving geometric consistency.

papers.abstract: Frontier coding agents are becoming increasingly adept at 3D modeling. Yet, they still face challenges when building objects meant to be assembled in the physical world, often creating invalid assemblies with floating, colliding, or disconnected parts. We argue that providing agents with tools for assembling builds and verifying their physical feasibility is sufficient for them to produce physically valid assemblies that still adhere to input prompts. Focusing on the domain of LEGO brick builds, we present BrickWright, a framework for generating physically feasible brick builds from text or image prompts using pre-trained agents, where a build is physically feasible if it uses only real parts, has no colliding or floating parts, and forms a connected structure if possible. BrickWright guides agents to create builds by writing code with BrickLayer, a Python toolkit with two main components: an ergonomic brick assembly API that halves inference cost compared to working in raw LDraw, and a validator that provides feedback on physical feasibility. Whereas baseline agents achieve physical validity rates ranging from only 9% (GPT-6 Luna) to 69% (GPT-6 Astra), BrickWright-guided agents achieve 100% validity on a sample of 512 prompts, while improving prompt adherence for lightweight agents and maintaining it for stronger agents. Additionally, they outperform specialized models on the text-to-brick task. Code is available on our project page: https://avalovelace1.github.io/brickwright/
authors: Ava Pun, Kevin Dai, Sally Chen, Maxwell Jones, Ruixuan Liu, Kangle Deng, Changliu Liu, Maneesh Agrawala, Deva Ramanan, Jun-Yan Zhu
bullets: Targets invalid 3D assemblies containing floating, colliding, disconnected, or unreal LEGO parts.
Uses BrickLayer, a Python toolkit with an ergonomic assembly API and a physical-feasibility validator.
The API halves inference cost compared with working directly in raw LDraw.
BrickWright-guided agents reached 100% validity on 512 prompts, versus 9–69% for baseline agents.
Improves prompt adherence for lightweight agents, maintains it for stronger agents, and outperforms specialized text-to-brick models.
papers.selection_reason: Generating physically feasible 3D brick builds from prompts fits 3D geometry generation.
papers.title: BrickWright: Agentic Creation of Physically Feasible Brick Builds
papers.tldr: BrickWright enables coding agents to generate LEGO builds that are physically feasible and faithful to text or image prompts by combining an assembly toolkit with validation feedback.

papers.abstract: Single-image 3D generation has achieved high fidelity on curated benchmarks, yet degrades sharply on real-world images with uneven illumination, blur, and occlusions. Purifying such inputs requires deciding when to intervene and preserving the visual cues needed for 3D generation, while leaving clean inputs unchanged. We introduce Gate3DGen, a selective pre-processing model that gates image inputs to existing 3D generators without retraining them. A degradation-aware router bypasses inputs classified as clean and extracts features to guide purification of the remaining inputs. Conditioned on these features, a 3D-oriented one-step purifier purifies degraded inputs with spatial losses that encourage preservation of object identity, contours, and textural cues. To provide paired supervision, we construct a synthetic data engine that renders clean views of 3D assets and synthesises composite degradations. On the synthetic benchmark, the purifier improves image fidelity and downstream 3D geometry in only 2.3s on average, reducing TRELLIS.2 mesh distance by 61.5% relative to degraded inputs. VLM evaluation and human preferences on real photographs further support identity preservation and degradation correction. More demos and code are available at https://supra-3d.github.io/gate3dgen.
authors: Xiaolin Li, Zihao Huang, Fanpeng Meng, Chen Yang, Guanjun Wu, Kai Zhang, Jiemin Fang, Qi Tian
bullets: Targets failures caused by uneven illumination, blur, and occlusions in real-world images.
Uses a degradation-aware router to decide whether to bypass or purify each input.
A one-step, 3D-oriented purifier preserves object identity, contours, and texture through spatial losses.
Synthetic paired data comes from rendered clean views combined with composite degradations.
On a synthetic benchmark, it reduces TRELLIS.2 mesh distance by 61.5% versus degraded inputs, with 2.3-second average processing; real-image evaluations support identity preservation.
papers.selection_reason: Selective purification of real-world images for 3D generation directly fits 3D vision.
papers.title: Gate3DGen: A Pre-processing Model that Selectively Purifies Real-World Images for 3D Generation
papers.tldr: Gate3DGen selectively purifies degraded real-world images before 3D generation while bypassing clean inputs, improving downstream geometry without retraining the generator.

papers.abstract: Monocular models recover 3D geometry from a single image in one pass, but most assume a pinhole camera and produce distorted geometry on the wide-angle imagery produced by fisheye and panoramic lenses. Camera-aware models remove this assumption by predicting a per-pixel ray field. However, they represent different camera geometries using a single fixed basis to capture both the overall camera projection and its finer variations. We argue that camera geometry can be viewed as having a hierarchy of complexity for representing rays. We present OmniRay, a feed-forward model whose Ray Module is composed of three components: a monotone radial base that captures radially symmetric structure, a spherical-harmonic residual for smooth deviations from it, and a free-form residual for remaining local variation. These components are composed as successive rotations on the sphere, allowing the representation to accommodate diverse camera geometries. Given a single image, OmniRay predicts a ray direction and an up-to-scale radial distance for every pixel, from which a 3D point cloud is recovered without needing camera information at inference time. Extensive experiments across different camera configurations demonstrate that OmniRay establishes a new state-of-the-art in camera-agnostic monocular 3D reconstruction.
authors: Namitha Guruprasad, Abhay Yadav, Cheng Peng, Rama Chellappa, Anand Bhattad
bullets: Addresses distortions caused by applying pinhole-camera assumptions to fisheye and panoramic imagery.
Uses a hierarchical Ray Module with a monotone radial base, spherical-harmonic residual, and free-form residual.
Represents these components as successive rotations on the sphere to model both global camera geometry and local variation.
Predicts per-pixel ray directions and up-to-scale radial distances for 3D point-cloud recovery.
Experiments across varied camera configurations report state-of-the-art camera-agnostic monocular 3D reconstruction.
papers.selection_reason: Camera-agnostic monocular 3D reconstruction directly fits 3D vision.
papers.title: OmniRay: Camera-Agnostic Monocular 3D Reconstruction with Composite Ray Fields
papers.tldr: OmniRay reconstructs 3D point clouds from a single image across diverse camera types without requiring camera information at inference time.

papers.abstract: Feed-forward models accurately estimate camera motion and 3D geometry from short video windows. However, computational and memory costs prevent direct inference on sequences containing thousands of frames. Long videos must therefore be processed as overlapping chunks. This division produces independent local reconstructions with inconsistent coordinate frames and duplicate estimates of shared cameras. Achieving global consistency requires propagating constraints from adjacent overlaps and distant revisits across the sequence. This requirement naturally motivates pose graph optimization. However, the choice of graph level creates a trade-off. Chunk-level graphs efficiently resolve scale drift and close large loops. Yet, their rigid transformations cannot correct internal errors or conflicting frame predictions. Conversely, frame-level optimization offers local flexibility, but scaling it globally is computationally expensive and can break metric scale. HiP3R resolves this trade-off using a hierarchical pose graph. HiP3R first optimizes a robust chunk-level $\mathrm{Sim}(3)$ graph to establish the global layout and scale. It then holds this layout fixed and estimates one shared $\mathrm{SE}(3)$ camera per frame, turning overlapping window predictions into a single trajectory. Experiments across multiple benchmarks demonstrate the effectiveness of HiP3R in improving camera trajectories and 3D reconstruction. Our method applies to both chunk-based and streaming backends without additional training or fine-tuning. The codes are available at https://kkakkkka.github.io/HiP3R.
authors: Zunnan Xu, Shangchen Zhou, Yihang Luo, Chen Change Loy
bullets: Long sequences processed in overlapping chunks yield inconsistent coordinate frames and duplicate camera estimates.
A robust chunk-level Sim(3) graph establishes global layout, scale, and loop consistency.
A subsequent frame-level SE(3) optimization produces one shared camera trajectory while preserving the global layout.
Experiments on multiple benchmarks improve camera trajectories and 3D reconstruction.
The method works with chunk-based and streaming backends without additional training or fine-tuning.
papers.selection_reason: Hierarchical pose graph optimization for long-horizon 3D reconstruction.
papers.title: HiP3R: Hierarchical Pose Graphs for Long-Horizon 3D Reconstruction
papers.tldr: HiP3R combines chunk- and frame-level pose-graph optimization to make long-video 3D reconstructions globally consistent and computationally practical.

papers.abstract: This paper studies category-level RGB-D object pose estimation, which recovers an object's 3D rotation and translation without instance-specific CAD models or reference views. This task is highly ambiguous due to intra-class variations, symmetries, and partial observations. Current solutions struggle to balance reliability and efficiency: methods based on intermediate structures are prone to error propagation, while diffusion models suffer from high inference latency and complex post-hoc candidate extraction. To address this, we present F2G-Pose, a real-time direct, single-pass framework that predicts category-level pose, metric size, and camera-frame completed shape from a single RGB-D observation in one feed-forward pass. F2G-Pose lifts dense visual foundation features to partial point clouds, encodes local geometry with DGCNN tokenization, and integrates object-level structure with a Mixture-of-Experts Transformer. Joint size prediction and camera-frame shape completion encourage metric consistency through dense geometric supervision. With its task-specific network trained only on pose-annotated synthetic SOPE data and its frozen RADIO backbone externally pretrained, F2G-Pose achieves state-of-the-art accuracy on SOPE and ROPE while running at 28 FPS for pose-only inference, and further demonstrates strong camera-frame geometry on HouseCat6D and real-object transfer on HANDAL. Analyses of latency, robustness, shape completion, and GenPose++ candidate behavior further demonstrate the efficiency and reliability of F2G-Pose, with real-world manipulation experiments demonstrating deployment potential under segmented RGB-D inputs. The project page, code, and pretrained models are made available at https://jrryzh.github.io/F2G-Pose/.
authors: Jinyu Zhang, Haitao Lin, Jiashu Hou, Xiangyang Xue, Yanwei Fu
bullets: Addresses ambiguity from intra-class variation, symmetries, and partial observations without instance CAD models or reference views.
Lifts frozen visual foundation features onto partial point clouds, models local geometry with DGCNN, and captures object structure using a Mixture-of-Experts Transformer.
Joint size prediction and camera-frame shape completion provide dense geometric supervision and metric consistency.
Reports state-of-the-art accuracy on SOPE and ROPE, with pose-only inference at 28 FPS; additional evaluations cover geometry, robustness, and real-object transfer.
Scope includes segmented RGB-D inputs and task-specific training on pose-annotated synthetic SOPE data.
papers.selection_reason: RGB-D category-level pose estimation with foundation features; relevant to 3D perception and robotic manipulation.
papers.title: F2G-Pose: Geometry-Aware Foundation Feature Lifting for Direct RGB-D Category-Level Object Pose Estimation
papers.tldr: F2G-Pose is a real-time, single-pass RGB-D framework that jointly predicts category-level object pose, size, and completed shape from one observation.

papers.abstract: Point cloud transformers aim to capture detailed local geometry and relationships across a scene at a manageable computational cost. Two common approaches are window attention and global attention. They differ in how they enable scene-wide interaction, which refers to information exchange among tokens across a scene. Window attention reduces computational cost by restricting self-attention to groups of tokens called windows; in serialized designs, each window contains a fixed number of consecutive tokens from a spatially ordered sequence. Because each block only directly connects tokens within the same window, information exchange across windows relies on changes in window membership across blocks and hierarchical pooling. Global attention, in contrast, directly connects all tokens within a scene, but computing attention over all token pairs can be costly when the number of tokens is large. To balance computational cost and scene-wide interaction, we introduce MixPT, a point transformer that uses a mix of window and global attention blocks in an interleaved schedule, while retaining a single fixed serialization pattern for its window blocks. For scenes with a large number of tokens, MixPT applies global attention to spatially pooled tokens and returns residual updates to the original-resolution stream. Across indoor and outdoor benchmarks, MixPT achieves competitive accuracy with lower latency than representative window and global attention baselines. We further demonstrate the feasibility of scaling the attention stage in depth by repeating the interleaved pattern of window and global attention blocks.
authors: Minkyun Seo, Hyungtae Lim, Jaesik Park
bullets: Window attention lowers cost but limits direct communication across windows; global attention enables scene-wide interaction but is expensive for large token sets.
MixPT interleaves window and global attention blocks while keeping one fixed serialization pattern for window processing.
For large scenes, global attention operates on spatially pooled tokens and sends residual updates back to the original-resolution stream.
Experiments on indoor and outdoor benchmarks show competitive accuracy with lower latency than representative window- and global-attention baselines.
The interleaved attention pattern can be repeated to scale the attention stage in depth.
papers.selection_reason: Point transformer with interleaved window and global attention, contributing to efficient attention and 3D point cloud processing.
papers.title: MixPT: Point Transformer with Interleaved Window and Global Attention
papers.tldr: MixPT balances local detail, global scene interaction, and efficiency by interleaving window and pooled-token global attention in a point transformer.

papers.abstract: Local feature matching is typically formulated for image pairs, although structure-from-motion and visual localization commonly match one reference image against many retrieved or covisible neighbours. Applying a pairwise matcher independently to these centre-neighbour edges duplicates reference-side computation and prevents the matcher from exploiting complementary multi-view geometric evidence from the remaining observations. To address these limitations, we introduce MVLoMa, a sparse star-graph matcher that extends LoMa from image pairs to multiple views. MVLoMa first uses a frozen multi-view geometry model to jointly describe all images in a star, then injects the resulting cross-view geometric context into local descriptors. It then matches the centre image to all neighbours in a single forward pass through per-view self-attention and bidirectional centre-neighbour cross-attention. For supervision, we derive positive correspondences only from depth-valid, mutually visible dense warps and explicitly penalize high-confidence matches that violate epipolar geometry. On 25-view star graphs from HyperSim, ScanNet++, Mip-NeRF 360, and Tanks and Temples, MVLoMa obtains the best macro-average relative-pose AUC among the compared methods at all three thresholds (58.65/85.41/90.99). Its matcher is 2.20 times faster than sequential evaluation of the 24 centre-neighbour edges. The same design supports four tested frozen geometry encoders -- DA3, $\pi^3$, VGGT, and VGGT-$\Omega$ -- with DA3-Giant performing best on all reported encoder-ablation metrics. Controlled ablations further isolate the effects of geometry-aware descriptors, visibility filtering, geometric negative supervision, and joint multi-view inference.
authors: Xinyang Lu, Shengzhe Wei, Sheng Tang, Weiqi Zhang, Juntong Fang, Zesong Li
bullets: Addresses redundant reference-image computation and missed cross-view geometric evidence in pairwise matching.
Uses a frozen multi-view geometry model, geometry-aware local descriptors, and joint centre-to-neighbour attention.
Trains with depth-valid, mutually visible correspondences and penalties for epipolar-violating high-confidence matches.
On 25-view star graphs across four datasets, it achieves the best reported macro-average relative-pose AUC at all thresholds.
Runs 2.20× faster than sequentially matching the 24 centre-neighbour pairs; the design works with four frozen geometry encoders.
papers.selection_reason: Multi-view local feature matching with geometry foundation models, contributing to 3D vision and geometric correspondence.
papers.title: MVLoMa: Multi-View Local Feature Matching with Any Geometry Foundation Model
papers.tldr: MVLoMa extends local feature matching from image pairs to multi-view star graphs, using shared geometry context for faster and more informed matching.

papers.abstract: 4D scene reconstruction requires robust handling of dynamic objects, yet existing streaming methods commonly assume static scenes, leading to pose drift and ghosting artifacts over long sequences. We introduce Stream4D, a training-free, motion-decoupled streaming reconstruction framework that can be directly integrated into causal Transformer backbones (e.g., StreamVGGT, Stream3R). Our key observation is that causal attention implicitly encodes rich temporal motion cues within the KV cache. We adaptively aggregate these cues from multiple attention layers and across temporal windows, and fuse them with depth priors to handle challenging cases such as occlusions and textureless regions, producing precise dynamic masks that decouple static and dynamic regions. We then apply a soft key masking scheme that leverages these dynamic masks to suppress interference from dynamic regions in causal attention, thereby improving camera pose estimation accuracy. Stream4D inherits the efficiency of causal attention and remains compatible with existing streaming architectures. On diverse dynamic-scene benchmarks, Stream4D significantly improves camera pose estimation and static-scene reconstruction quality, yields reliable dynamic masks, and effectively mitigates long-sequence ghosting.
authors: Wei Zhang, Ying Feng, Mengtong Wu, Shiqiang Gong, Huaqi Zhang, Qi Zhang
bullets: Addresses failures of static-scene assumptions in streaming reconstruction, especially long-sequence pose drift and ghosting.
Aggregates temporal motion cues from multiple causal-attention layers and windows, fusing them with depth priors to identify dynamic regions.
Uses soft key masking to suppress dynamic-region interference during camera pose estimation.
Integrates directly with causal Transformer backbones such as StreamVGGT and Stream3R while preserving streaming efficiency.
Improves camera poses, static-scene reconstruction, dynamic masks, and long-sequence ghosting on diverse dynamic-scene benchmarks.
papers.selection_reason: Streaming 4D reconstruction with motion decoupling via causal KV-cache attention, relevant to 3D/4D scene perception.
papers.title: Stream4D: Streaming 4D Reconstruction with Training-free Motion Decoupling via Causal KV-Cache Attention
papers.tldr: Stream4D enables training-free streaming 4D reconstruction by extracting motion cues from causal KV caches to separate dynamic regions and reduce pose drift and ghosting.

papers.abstract: LiDAR point cloud semantic segmentation is a fundamental component of 3D perception for autonomous driving and robotics. Projection-based methods map 3D point clouds into 2D representations for feature extraction using 2D networks. However, aggregating multiple points during projection can obscure geometric differences within each frustum, while local feature extraction limits the modeling of spatial relationships across scanning regions. Moreover, proximity in the projected representation does not necessarily imply proximity in 3D space, and interactions between point and projected features may mix features from different ranges, reducing semantic discriminability. To address these challenges, we propose the Ray-aligned and Scan-aware Fusion Network (RaSFNet), which incorporates point cloud geometry and LiDAR scanning characteristics into projection-based semantic segmentation. Specifically, the Ray-Aligned Geometric Distribution Encoding (RAGDE) module characterizes point distributions within each frustum using a ray-aligned coordinate system. To model spatial context, a Scan-Topology-Aware Mamba (STAM) block organizes frustum features according to the LiDAR azimuth sampling pattern and captures long-range dependencies across scanning regions. In addition, a Range-Constrained Point-Frustum Fusion (RCPFF) mechanism uses shared range information to guide feature exchange between point and frustum representations while maintaining spatial correspondence. RaSFNet achieves mIoU scores of 70.2% and 77.7% on the SemanticKITTI and nuScenes validation sets, respectively, indicating competitive segmentation performance compared with the evaluated methods.
bullets: Addresses geometric information loss within projected frustums and limited spatial-context modeling in 2D representations.
RAGDE encodes point distributions using a ray-aligned coordinate system.
STAM captures long-range dependencies according to LiDAR azimuth scanning patterns.
RCPFF uses shared range information to preserve correspondence during point–frustum feature fusion.
Reports 70.2% mIoU on SemanticKITTI and 77.7% on nuScenes validation sets, with competitive performance against evaluated methods.
papers.selection_reason: LiDAR semantic segmentation with ray-aligned geometric encoding and scan-aware fusion.
papers.title: RaSFNet: Ray-aligned and Scan-aware Fusion Network for LiDAR Semantic Segmentation
papers.tldr: RaSFNet improves projection-based LiDAR semantic segmentation by combining ray-aligned geometry, scan-aware context modeling, and range-constrained point–frustum fusion.

papers.abstract: Generative modeling for Computer-Aided Design (CAD) remains fundamentally challenged by the need to capture the intricate interplay between discrete topological connectivity and precise spatial geometry inherent in Boundary Representations (B-reps). Existing generative approaches largely formulate CAD construction as a sequence modeling problem, but consequently lack an explicit topological inductive bias. In this work, we present GraphCAD, a geometry-aware generative framework that centers modeling on the Edge-Adjacency Graph (EAG), a novel graph-based CAD representation tailored for generative tasks. GraphCAD adopts a hybrid graph diffusion formulation to jointly model the discrete and continuous components of EAG and introduces a geometry-aware denoising mechanism that renders node attributes into spatial point sets. These point sets are encoded by an SE(3)-equivariant backbone and fused into the node representations, thereby grounding the generative process in physical geometry. To support this study, we construct EAGBench, a large-scale dataset of engineering CAD models. Extensive experiments show that GraphCAD can generate complex CAD models with more than 50 faces and achieves state-of-the-art performance in geometric fidelity and distributional alignment compared with sequence-based baselines.
authors: Wenhao Zheng, Xianggen Liu, Li Yue, Jiancheng Shi, Jiancheng Lv
bullets: Targets the challenge of jointly modeling B-rep topology and precise spatial geometry.
Introduces EAG, a graph-based CAD representation designed for generative modeling.
Uses hybrid graph diffusion for discrete connectivity and continuous node attributes.
Renders node attributes as point sets and encodes them with an SE(3)-equivariant backbone for geometry-aware denoising.
Evaluations on the newly constructed EAGBench show strong geometric fidelity and distributional alignment, including models with over 50 faces.
papers.selection_reason: Geometry-aware graph diffusion for CAD B-rep generation directly contributes to 3D generative modeling.
papers.title: GraphCAD: Geometry-Aware Diffusion on Edge-Adjacency Graphs for CAD Generation
papers.tldr: GraphCAD generates complex CAD models by combining edge-adjacency graphs with geometry-aware hybrid diffusion.

papers.abstract: Neurosurgical navigation commonly presents magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) as 2D slices, making it difficult to relate the anatomy in those slices to the cortical surface observed through the surgical microscope. We seek a common 3D visualization that combines a photorealistic reconstruction of the exposed cortex during tumor surgery with whole-brain MRI context and diffusion tractography pathways. This requires the reconstructed cortex to form a clear boundary around the brain anatomy rather than a diffuse volume that obscures internal structures. Conventional 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) can reproduce observed views but, under limited surgical view coverage, may distribute opacity through a thick and geometrically ambiguous band. We introduce height-field 2D Gaussian Splatting (H-2DGS), a three-stage pipeline that concentrates a robust 3DGS reconstruction, fuses its depth into a shared truncated signed distance field (TSDF) surface, and represents that surface with curved, surface-oriented Gaussian primitives. Separate height, color, and opacity bases provide local geometry and appearance, while a neighbor-transition objective coordinates overlapping patches. The explicit surface further supports postoperative alignment: MRI-derived depth deforms the reconstruction, and tracked-color supervision with alternating optimization preserves its appearance. Across five real neurosurgical cases, H-2DGS gives low multi-view depth inconsistency, a compact 7.97MB representation, and interactive rendering at 29--42ms per frame. The resulting sharp, deformable surface integrates clearly with tractography and MRI anatomy, including a postoperative resection cavity.
authors: Zhang Zichuan, Bart Brouwers, Rembrandt Bakker, Maud Landers, Geert-Jan Rutten, Maxime Chamberland
bullets: Addresses the ambiguity of conventional 3D Gaussian Splatting, which can produce diffuse volumetric reconstructions of exposed cortex.
Uses a three-stage pipeline: robust 3DGS initialization, TSDF-based surface fusion, and curved surface-oriented Gaussian primitives.
Separates height, color, and opacity representations and uses neighbor-transition optimization to improve continuity across patches.
Supports postoperative deformation through MRI-derived depth and preserves appearance with tracked-color supervision.
Validated on five real neurosurgical cases, achieving low multi-view depth inconsistency, a 7.97MB representation, and interactive 29–42 ms rendering.
papers.selection_reason: Presents a structured 3D Gaussian splatting surface reconstruction method with TSDF fusion, relevant to 3D vision.
papers.title: H-2DGS: Height-Field Gaussian Splatting for Sharp and Deformable Neurosurgical Surface Reconstruction
papers.tldr: H-2DGS reconstructs a sharp, deformable cortical surface from limited surgical views and integrates it with MRI and tractography for neurosurgical navigation.

papers.abstract: Lifting vision-language features such as CLIP into 3D Gaussian reconstructions enables open-vocabulary segmentation through natural-language queries. Although CLIP represents a broad range of semantic concepts, the lifted features of individual scenes can exhibit strong directional concentration, while raw cosine similarity does not account for the scene-specific feature distribution. We show that substantial segmentation gains can be obtained by changing how a fixed lifted feature field is compared with text. Our method partially subtracts a shared scene direction from visual features and text prototypes and whitens text prototypes using a fixed reference vocabulary of generic terms. It then uses soft clustering for multiclass prediction and CSLS with a relevance margin against the reference vocabulary for single-query prediction. Beyond reducing directional concentration, scene centering improves class-relative feature separation in every evaluated scene. Across seven lifting methods and four datasets, the resulting query-time calibration consistently improves mean intersection over union in both multiclass and single-query segmentation. These gains require no retraining, source-image re-encoding, or feature re-lifting, demonstrating the value of scene-conditioned comparison for making better use of existing lifted representations.
authors: Dominik Engel, Yousef Rajeh, Leon Sick, Ivan Viola
bullets: Addresses scene-specific directional concentration that makes raw CLIP cosine similarity unreliable for 3D segmentation.
Partially removes a shared scene direction and whitens text prototypes using a fixed vocabulary of generic terms.
Uses soft clustering for multiclass prediction and CSLS with a relevance margin for single-query prediction.
Improves class-relative feature separation across evaluated scenes and consistently raises mean IoU across seven lifting methods and four datasets.
Operates entirely at query time, requiring no retraining, source-image re-encoding, or feature re-lifting.
papers.selection_reason: Open-vocabulary 3D segmentation with CLIP feature calibration.
papers.title: Query-Time Calibration of CLIP Features for Open-Vocabulary 3D Segmentation
papers.tldr: A query-time calibration scheme improves open-vocabulary 3D segmentation from fixed CLIP-based feature fields without retraining or re-lifting features.

papers.abstract: Relighting and novel view synthesis of human portraits are essential in applications such as portrait photography, virtual reality (VR), and augmented reality (AR). Despite recent progress, 3D-aware portrait relighting remains challenging due to the demands for photorealistic rendering, real-time performance, and generalization to unseen subjects. Existing works either rely on supervision from limited and expensive light stage captured data or produce suboptimal results. Moreover, many works are based on generative NeRFs, which suffer from poor 3D consistency and low real-time performance. We resort to recent progress on generative 3D Gaussians and design a lighting model based on a unified neural radiance transfer representation, which responds linearly to incident light. Using only in-the-wild images, our method achieves state-of-the-art relighting results and a significantly faster rendering speed ($\times12$) compared to previous 3D-aware portrait relighting research. Project page: http://www.geometrylearning.com/GSHeadRelight/.
authors: Henglei Lv, Bailin Deng, Jianzhu Guo, Xiaoqiang Liu, Pengfei Wan, Di Zhang, Lin Gao
bullets: Targets 3D-aware portrait relighting and novel-view synthesis for VR, AR, and photography.
Uses generative 3D Gaussians instead of generative NeRFs to improve 3D consistency and real-time performance.
Introduces a unified neural radiance transfer lighting model with a linear response to incident light.
Requires only in-the-wild images, avoiding reliance on limited and expensive light-stage supervision.
Reports state-of-the-art relighting and 12× faster rendering than prior 3D-aware portrait-relighting methods.
papers.selection_reason: Fast relightable 3D Gaussian head synthesis from in-the-wild images; relevant to 3D vision and generative 3D scene modeling.
papers.title: GSHeadRelight: Fast Relightability for 3D Gaussian Head Synthesis
papers.tldr: GSHeadRelight enables fast, photorealistic, and generalizable relighting of 3D Gaussian human heads using only in-the-wild images.

papers.abstract: We introduce Foundation4D, a unified feed-forward model for geometry estimation, 3D detection, semantic occupancy, and Gaussian reconstruction from multi-camera driving video. A shared backbone uses factorized spatiotemporal attention to efficiently combine observations across cameras and time. Our video inference pipeline uses pose graph optimization to refine camera trajectories and assembles object tracks across input windows. We also develop a data annotation pipeline and release PAI-Foundation4D, a benchmark with dense depth and semantic occupancy labels for 1,253 driving clips. With benchmark-specific fine-tuning, Foundation4D achieves the lowest depth AbsRel on Waymo and nuScenes, the highest detection mAP on nuScenes, and the highest occupancy mIoU on OpenOccupancy among the compared methods. Our task-combination study shows benefits for both detection and geometry: co-training detection with geometry and occupancy improves top-class mAP by 1.2 points over detection-only training, while co-training geometry with detection reduces camera-to-rig translation error by $13.4\%$ relative to geometry-only training. We further use the predicted geometry and trajectories as priors for lidarless NuRec, supporting reconstruction of driving scenes for simulation.
authors: NVIDIA, :, S\'ergio Agostinho, Maximilian Apodaca, Emmanuel Attia, Guillem Braso, George Dong, Ilya Fedorov, Michele Fenzi, Gang Huang, Jiahui Huang, Shengyu Huang, Bingxin Ke, Laura Leal-Taix\'e, Kuan-Ting Lee, Mingxuan Liu, Tian Liu, Tim Meinhardt, Aljo\v{s}a O\v{s}ep, Naveen Kumar Rai, Kefei Ren, Cristiano Saltori, Keqiang Wu, Ning Xu, Fei Xue, Jin-Bey Yu, Lei Zhang, Qunjie Zhou
bullets: Addresses geometry estimation, 3D detection, semantic occupancy, and Gaussian reconstruction in one feed-forward model.
Uses a shared backbone with factorized spatiotemporal attention to fuse camera and temporal observations efficiently.
Refines camera trajectories with pose-graph optimization and assembles object tracks across video windows.
Introduces PAI-Foundation4D, a benchmark with dense depth and semantic occupancy labels for 1,253 driving clips.
Reports leading compared performance on Waymo depth, nuScenes detection, and OpenOccupancy occupancy; supports lidarless scene reconstruction for simulation.
papers.selection_reason: Unified 3D perception and reconstruction model for autonomous vehicles, combining geometry, detection, occupancy, and Gaussian reconstruction; strong 3D vision and embodied-perception relevance.
papers.title: Foundation4D: Towards a unified perception and reconstruction model for autonomous vehicles
papers.tldr: Foundation4D unifies multi-camera video perception and 3D scene reconstruction for autonomous driving, achieving strong results across depth, detection, and occupancy benchmarks.

papers.abstract: Generating an articulated object from a single image requires recovering both its appearance and the mechanism governing its parts. A compact encoding of joint attributes does not by itself ensure that reconstruction preserves the resulting motion. We present MoRE, Motion-Regularized Encoding for articulated 3D generation. MoRE represents coordinate-aligned joint lines with axis classification and two axis-orthogonal Pl\"ucker moment coefficients, removing the arbitrary choice of an origin along the axis. During representation learning, decoded joint hypotheses are used to move corresponding three-dimensional anchors, and their motions are compared with those of annotated joints. A differentiable expectation over joint types and axis directions couples attribute reconstruction to the motion it induces. An image-conditioned flow learns the resulting functional latents, while a multi-state-adapted Gaussian model supplies appearance. At inference, recovered part assignments and joints articulate a single set of rest-pose Gaussians without regenerating the object for each state. Experiments on PartNet-Mobility and ACD show stronger part-box agreement, articulated-state geometry and visual similarity than the compared baselines, while joint prediction reduces axis, origin and range errors relative to ArtiLatent. Controlled ablations support the joint-line encoding and show that motion supervision reduces anchor-motion error. Code and pretrained checkpoints will be released in the future.
