bullets: Represents joints using axis classification and axis-orthogonal Plücker moment coefficients, avoiding arbitrary axis-origin choices.
Uses decoded joint hypotheses to move 3D anchors and matches those motions to annotated joints through differentiable motion supervision.
Combines image-conditioned functional latents with a multi-state Gaussian appearance model.
Articulates one set of rest-pose Gaussians across states instead of regenerating the object for each pose.

On PartNet-Mobility and ACD, improves part-box, articulated-state geometry, visual similarity, and joint-prediction errors over compared baselines; ablations support the encoding and motion supervision.
papers.selection_reason: Articulated 3D generation from a single image with joint-line encoding and motion-supervised representation learning; core 3D geometry and generation contribution.
papers.title: MoRE: Motion-Regularized Encoding for Articulated 3D Generation
papers.tldr: MoRE generates articulated 3D objects from a single image by encoding joint lines and explicitly regularizing the motion they induce.

papers.abstract: Dynamic representations based on 4D Gaussian Splatting (4DGS) have shown strong capabilities in reconstruction and rendering, yet current methods remain limited in supporting complex natural-language referring in dynamic scenes. Existing 4D Gaussian methods are primarily designed for rendering-oriented dynamic modeling, while current semantic extensions often rely on scene-specific semantic optimization or are evaluated on relatively simple query settings. In this paper, we study Referring 4D Gaussian Splatting (R4DGS), a task for grounding temporally varying, multi-target or reasoning-intensive, and zero-target or distractor expressions in dynamic 4D scenes. To support this task, we introduce R4D-Bench-QA, a benchmark with structured query annotations. We further present ReferGaussian, a unified framework built upon 4DGS that converts low-level dynamic Gaussians into persistent, language-addressable entities for training-free referring inference. ReferGaussian organizes mask-supported Gaussian entities in an EntityBank, uses Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) to decompose complex queries into trackable object phrases and structured referring constraints, and performs constraint-aware grounding without scene-specific semantic optimization. Experiments on R4D-Bench-QA and the 4D LangSplat protocol demonstrate improved temporal target selection and competitive spatiotemporal grounding without scene-specific semantic training. Project resources are available at https://chenbangpu.github.io/R4DGS/.
authors: Bangpu Chen, Yaxuan Li, Shirui Peng, Xiangtian Si, Liuxin Chu, Xitong Cao, Hongbo Jin, Jiayu Ding
bullets: Addresses temporal, multi-target, reasoning-intensive, and zero-target or distractor referring expressions in dynamic 4D scenes.
Introduces R4D-Bench-QA with structured query annotations for evaluating referring segmentation.
ReferGaussian converts dynamic Gaussians into persistent language-addressable entities stored in an EntityBank.
MLLMs decompose queries into object phrases and referring constraints, enabling constraint-aware grounding without scene-specific semantic optimization.
Shows improved temporal target selection and competitive spatiotemporal grounding on R4D-Bench-QA and the 4D LangSplat protocol.
papers.selection_reason: Grounds referring language in dynamic 4D Gaussian scenes via MLLM-guided decomposition and spatial entity grounding; directly relevant to spatial intelligence and 3D vision.
papers.title: R4DGS: Referring Segmentation in 4D Gaussian Splatting
papers.tldr: R4DGS introduces a benchmark and training-free framework for grounding complex language references to dynamic objects in 4D Gaussian Splatting scenes.

papers.abstract: We introduce EgoHand, a monocular 3D hand reconstruction model that achieves state-of-the-art performance on egocentric video. Central to our approach is the curation of a high-quality training corpus of 14 million images, combining synthetic data, in-the-wild video, and multi-camera motion capture to balance scene diversity and supervision quality. The model adopts SOMA-Hand as its parametric representation and processes 2D hand crops with a transformer encoder, incorporating camera cues and an auxiliary 2D branch to improve geometric consistency and image alignment. Zero-shot evaluations on HOT3D, ARCTIC, and H2O demonstrate strong out-of-domain generalization, with lower joint-position, root-translation, and acceleration errors than competing baselines at an inference latency of approximately 9.69 ms. A blinded user preference study further shows that participants favor EgoHand's reconstructed hand poses over those from Apple EgoDex and Ropedia Xperience-10M. We release the EgoHand model and source code under the OpenMDW license, allowing free commercial use of the model.
authors: Chao-Yeh Chen, Tiffany Chen, Lin Duan, Tianyi Hu, Yu-Hsiang Huang, Umar Iqbal, Jiefeng Li, Edy Lim, Yanchen Liu, Yihan Pang, Hang Qiu, Jun Saito, Shao Su, Qingsi Wang, Xiufeng Xie
bullets: Addresses accurate 3D hand reconstruction from challenging egocentric video.
Trains on a 14-million-image corpus combining synthetic, in-the-wild, and multi-camera motion-capture data.
Uses SOMA-Hand with a transformer encoder, camera cues, and an auxiliary 2D branch for geometric and image consistency.
Performs strongly on zero-shot HOT3D, ARCTIC, and H2O evaluations, with approximately 9.69 ms inference latency.
Model and source code are released under the OpenMDW license with free commercial use.
papers.selection_reason: Introduces EgoHand, a monocular 3D hand reconstruction model trained on egocentric video. This falls under 3D Vision and involves learning from human videos, which is relevant to embodied AI and 3D perception.
papers.title: EgoHand: Monocular 3D Hand Reconstruction from Egocentric Video
papers.tldr: EgoHand reconstructs 3D hands from monocular egocentric video using diverse training data and camera-aware transformer modeling, achieving strong zero-shot generalization and fast inference.

papers.abstract: A patient who has lost part of the skull vault needs an implant that fits the defect exactly, and such implants are still drawn by hand in CAD by specialists, which makes each case slow and expensive. The task can be considered as a shape completion problem, so pretrained completion models, and now the first shape completion foundation models, look like a way to remove that manual step. We audited three publicly released pretrained shape completion models, two of them foundation models, applied zero-shot to 239 cranial defects, some carved from public skull datasets and some real post-craniectomy cases. Each output was compared with simply returning the patient's own remaining bone, and tested for whether the predicted material could be placed without intersecting the bone that is still there. On the 210 carved defects none of the three improved on doing nothing, and on the 29 real cases only one did so beyond chance. Yet not one output, from any model in any configuration, was implantable: none managed both to stay clear of the bone the patient still has and to place more material than doing nothing, where a task-specific volumetric model, trained for this task and selected on these cases, was implantable on all but one. The output that most convincingly resembles a skull is no more placeable than the rest, and at these point densities implant thickness cannot be read off the emitted points at all, which is a property of the output representation rather than of any one model. On this evidence the shape completion foundation models we could obtain cannot be trusted and, used as released, are not usable in clinical practice. Substantial research towards trustworthy foundation models for shape completion is still needed.
authors: Marek Wodzinski, Kamil Kwarciak, Daria Hemmerling, Mateusz Daniol
bullets: Evaluated three pretrained models on 239 cranial defects, including carved synthetic defects and real post-craniectomy cases.
None outperformed simply using the patient’s remaining bone on 210 carved defects; only one improved beyond chance on 29 real cases.
No model output was implantable because predictions failed to both avoid existing bone and add useful material.
A task-specific volumetric model was implantable on all but one case, indicating the limitation is not inherent to the task.
At the tested point densities, emitted points cannot reliably determine implant thickness, highlighting a representation-level limitation.
papers.selection_reason: Audits pretrained 3D shape completion foundation models for cranial defect reconstruction; directly addresses trustworthiness and usability of 3D foundation models.
papers.title: Plausible but Unimplantable: A Trustworthiness Audit of Shape Completion Foundation Models for Cranial Defect Reconstruction
papers.tldr: An audit finds that publicly released shape-completion foundation models produce plausible-looking but clinically unimplantable cranial reconstructions in zero-shot use.

papers.abstract: This paper addresses the problem of creating immersive volumetric videos from sparse and low-resolution capture resources. Conventional dense multi-view reconstruction methods can produce high-quality volumetric videos, but their reliance on costly capture setups makes them impractical in real-world scenarios. Recent approaches use generative models to relax capture requirements, but still suffer from limited resolution and 4D inconsistency. To overcome these constraints, we propose RealMe, a unified framework built around a high-resolution video diffusion model that enhances limited captures into high-resolution (2K), 4D-consistent videos for volumetric video reconstruction. Specifically, RealMe constructs auxiliary data from capture videos and encodes them into latents along with layout-aware positional embeddings. The video diffusion model adapts factorized spatio-temporal attention to the multi-view capture layout, denoises these latents across viewpoints and time, and decodes them into enhanced videos to refine the 4D representation. This adaptation helps the model capture temporal dynamics and multi-view relationships, leading to more 4D-consistent generation. To reduce the data gap between generated videos and real captures, we apply a latent frequency loss that provides frequency-domain supervision in latent space. Extensive experiments on the public DNA-Rendering benchmark and our self-captured RealVV dataset demonstrate that RealMe is able to create immersive volumetric videos and outperforms state-of-the-art methods in visual fidelity and 4D consistency.
authors: Chenxu Zhou, Zhiyuan Yu, Yudong Jin, Yinji Shentu, Yu Zhang, Jiaming Sun, Xiaowei Zhou
bullets: Targets costly dense multi-view capture requirements and the limited resolution and 4D consistency of prior generative methods.
Builds auxiliary data from capture videos and combines latent representations with layout-aware positional embeddings.
Adapts factorized spatio-temporal attention to model relationships across viewpoints and time.
Uses latent frequency-domain supervision to reduce the gap between generated videos and real captures.
Experiments on DNA-Rendering and the self-captured RealVV dataset show improved visual fidelity and 4D consistency over existing methods.
papers.selection_reason: Unified video diffusion framework for enhancing sparse multi-view captures into 4D-consistent volumetric video; directly relevant to video diffusion and 3D video generation.
papers.title: RealMe: Immersive Volumetric Video from Minimal Captures
papers.tldr: RealMe uses a high-resolution video diffusion model to turn sparse, low-resolution captures into immersive, temporally and multi-view consistent volumetric videos.

papers.abstract: Language 3D Gaussian Splatting enables open-vocabulary scene understanding by associating Gaussian primitives with language features. These semantic attributes increase model storage, while most existing 3DGS compression methods are designed mainly to preserve RGB rendering quality. One straightforward approach is to apply sparsification and quantization sequentially. However, pruning based only on rendering quality can remove Gaussians that have small RGB contributions but are important for semantic prediction. Once removed, their semantic information cannot be recovered by later quantization. We propose ClunoGS, a compact framework for Language 3DGS that combines semantics-aware Gaussian sparsification and vector quantization in a unified constrained objective. Semantic supervision is used during sparsification, and the objective jointly considers rendering quality, semantic accuracy, and compactness. We optimize the unified objective with alternating primal, sparsification, quantization, and dual updates. We evaluate ClunoGS on open-vocabulary localization and segmentation using the LERF and ScanNet-10 benchmarks. Under aggressive compression, our unified, semantics-aware formulation substantially alleviates the degradation of semantic representations caused by sequential compression and semantics-agnostic Gaussian sparsification. Ablations further show that jointly coordinating sparsification and quantization better preserves semantic accuracy than applying them independently.
authors: Jian Xu, Yi Li, Ying Huang, Siyi Wu, Bingzhe Li, Yuede Ji, Miao Yin
bullets: Addresses the loss of important semantic information when RGB-focused Gaussian pruning is followed by quantization.
Combines semantics-aware Gaussian sparsification and vector quantization in one constrained objective.
Balances rendering quality, semantic accuracy, and compactness using alternating primal, sparsification, quantization, and dual updates.
Evaluated on open-vocabulary localization and segmentation with LERF and ScanNet-10.
Under aggressive compression, better preserves semantic representations than sequential or independently applied compression.
papers.selection_reason: Semantics-aware compression of language 3D Gaussian splatting; fits 3D vision and efficiency.
papers.title: ClunoGS: Compact Language 3D Gaussian Splatting via Unified Optimization
papers.tldr: ClunoGS compresses Language 3D Gaussian Splatting while preserving both visual rendering and semantic understanding through unified, semantics-aware optimization.

papers.abstract: Recovering metric world-space hand motion from egocentric video supports understanding human interactions and transferring them to embodied agents. Three challenges complicate this task: multi-stage pipelines propagate errors from independently estimated hand and camera motion; monocular observations leave physical scale ambiguous; and occlusion and out-of-view hands admit multiple plausible motion trajectories. We present DewHand, a unified model for direct joint reconstruction of world-space hand and camera motion. To avoid compounding errors from multi-stage estimation, DewHand jointly predicts hand and camera motion in a shared world coordinate system within a single-stage pipeline. To resolve metric-scale ambiguity, it combines scene-level geometric features from VGGT-$\Omega$ with metric-space supervision, while hand-specific features preserve fine-grained articulation. To handle occlusion and out-of-view hands, we formulate reconstruction as conditional motion generation with flow matching. Under the same architecture, this generative formulation outperforms direct regression in both accuracy and temporal smoothness with only two sampling steps. Experiments on HOT3D and ARCTIC demonstrate improved world-space accuracy and temporal consistency over state-of-the-art methods. DewHand reduces rigid-aligned world-space error relative to StableHand from 32.9 to 28.4 mm on HOT3D and from 76.2 to 36.2 mm on ARCTIC. It also recovers camera scale within 10% on two thirds of HOT3D clips, versus about a quarter for SLAM. Moreover, in zero-shot evaluations on HoloAssist, H2O, and TACO, captured with different devices, DewHand achieves the lowest rigid-aligned world-space error (WA-MPJPE) on each dataset.
authors: Naru Suzuki, Satoshi Ikehata, Takehiko Ohkawa, Yoichi Sato, Shuhei Kurita
bullets: Addresses error propagation, monocular scale ambiguity, and ambiguous motion from occlusion or out-of-view hands.
Uses a single-stage model that jointly predicts hand and camera motion in a shared world coordinate system.
Combines VGGT-Ω scene geometry, metric-space supervision, and hand-specific articulation features.
Flow-matching generation outperforms direct regression in accuracy and temporal smoothness with two sampling steps.
Improves world-space accuracy on HOT3D and ARCTIC, estimates camera scale within 10% on two thirds of HOT3D clips, and generalizes zero-shot across three datasets.
papers.selection_reason: Egocentric metric hand/camera motion reconstruction for embodied skill transfer; fits human-video learning and 3D perception.
papers.title: DewHand: Direct Metric World-Space Hand Motion Reconstruction from Egocentric Videos
papers.tldr: DewHand jointly reconstructs metrically scaled world-space hand and camera motion from egocentric video, using geometric and hand-specific features plus flow-matching generation to improve accuracy and temporal smoothness under occlusion.

papers.abstract: Many robotic construction applications, such as progress tracking, require registering a sensor trajectory to a prior 2D floor plan. Visual capture is attractive for its low cost and availability, but aligning a visual simultaneous localization and mapping (VSLAM) map to a floor plan is difficult; VSLAM recovers geometry only up to an unknown similarity transform, the sparse point cloud is cross-modal to the symbolic floor plan, sites are only partially built during capture, and construction sites are visually repetitive, degrading map quality while removing distinctive features. Existing methods address at most two of these challenges. We thus introduce Reading the Room(RR), a global-local approach to register scale-ambiguous, sparse, semantic VSLAM maps to partially built floor plans. Our key idea is to define a single robust, differentiable, class-balanced semantic-geometric energy function that governs all stages of the pipeline. We develop two global initialization schemes, leveraging a single inaccurate user-provided correspondence if provided, or estimating the initialization globally using a cross-modal matching network. Both schemes are designed to find initial candidates with respect to the energy function, which is then directly optimized for local refinement. We evaluate RR on 33 sequences across three active construction sites against classical and learning-based baselines, achieving a 4.5x improvement in mean absolute trajectory error over the strongest baseline in the general unconstrained setting, which increases to 7.6x when an anchor is provided.
authors: Bjorn Stragier, Emilia Szyma\'nska, J. Micah Prendergast, Lukas Rosenberger Schmid
bullets: Addresses unknown scale, cross-modal map alignment, incomplete construction, and repetitive visual environments.
Uses a robust, differentiable, class-balanced semantic-geometric energy function throughout the pipeline.
Initializes registration either from one inaccurate user correspondence or via a cross-modal matching network.
Globally finds candidate alignments, then directly optimizes the energy for local refinement.
Evaluated on 33 sequences across three construction sites, improving mean absolute trajectory error by 4.5× over the strongest baseline generally and 7.6× with an anchor.
papers.selection_reason: Semantic registration of sparse 3D VSLAM maps to floor plans is a 3D vision perception problem.
papers.title: Reading the Room: Scale-ambiguous Semantic Registration of Sparse VSLAM Maps to Floor Plans in Partially Built Environments
papers.tldr: Reading the Room registers sparse, scale-ambiguous semantic VSLAM maps to floor plans in partially built construction sites using a unified global-to-local optimization pipeline.

papers.abstract: Feed-forward visual geometry models, exemplified by VGGT, have demonstrated strong multi-view reconstruction capabilities through dense global attention. However, the resulting all-to-all cross-view computation scales quadratically with the number of input views, making long-sequence inference particularly expensive due to substantial frame-level redundancy among highly overlapping observations. We uncover a topology-first, geometry-later evolution in VGGT camera tokens: shallow-layer tokens reliably capture local view neighborhoods, whereas deeper-layer tokens progressively encode globally organized inter-view geometry. Motivated by this observation, we introduce BlazeVGGT, a training-free framework for structure-aware frame-level key--value sparsification. At each global-attention block, BlazeVGGT constructs a view-level similarity kernel from camera-token relations and employs greedy determinantal point process inference to select a compact set of mutually complementary views. The selected views constitute the key--value context, while all input frames are retained as queries. This asymmetric attention design preserves dense per-frame predictions while eliminating redundant cross-view computation, allowing our method to be directly integrated into pretrained VGGT as a plug-and-play module without parameter updates. Its advantages become increasingly pronounced with sequence length: at 2,000 frames, BlazeVGGT achieves approximately 13$\times$ faster inference than VGGT while reducing the Chamfer Distance from 0.41 to 0.32. Extensive experiments demonstrate a favorable accuracy--efficiency trade-off in point-cloud reconstruction and camera-pose estimation, compatibility with existing VGGT accelerators such as FastVGGT and LiteVGGT, and transferability to VGGT-based models including StreamVGGT and PAGE-4D. Codes are publicly available at https://github.com/MagiciannnY/BlazeVGGT.git.
authors: Shujun Yao, Junhui Lin, Congying Han, Tiande Guo, Ziwen Liu, Bonan Li
bullets: VGGT’s all-to-all attention becomes costly for long, highly overlapping image sequences.
The method uses camera-token similarities to identify local-to-global view structure across network layers.
Greedy determinantal point process selection chooses complementary frames as sparse key–value context, while retaining all frames as queries.
At 2,000 frames, inference is approximately 13× faster and Chamfer Distance decreases from 0.41 to 0.32.
The plug-and-play approach transfers to VGGT variants and supports point-cloud reconstruction and camera-pose estimation.
papers.selection_reason: Introduces BlazeVGGT, a training-free framework for sparsifying camera tokens in multi-view geometry models, fitting 3D Vision and Efficient AI.
papers.title: BlazeVGGT: 13x Faster VGGT at 2,000 Frames via Camera Token without Training
papers.tldr: BlazeVGGT makes VGGT about 13× faster on 2,000-frame sequences by sparsifying redundant cross-view attention without retraining, while improving reported reconstruction accuracy.

papers.abstract: Real-world physical sensing exhibits complex, heterogeneous noise patterns that deviate significantly from idealized simulation, posing a fundamental bottleneck for sim-to-real transfer. Existing sensor modelings typically treat depth noise as a monolithic black-box process, overlooking the distinct physical mechanisms that govern different error modalities. In this work, we introduce a physics-grounded paradigm that disentangles monolithic noise into two complementary modalities: \textbf{sensing invalidation} and \textbf{measurement inaccuracy}, enabling a tailored treatment of noise sources based on their physical origins. Building on this insight, we propose \textbf{PRISM}, a tripartite framework that distills 3D Visual Foundation Model features as rich spatial-semantic priors for physics-based reasoning. To address the inherent sparsity and class imbalance of invalidation regions, we develop Hierarchical Positive-Prioritized Supervision, integrating multi-scale positive-weighted objectives with a positive-preserving dynamic hard mining strategy to enforce precise artifact delineation. Extensive benchmarks demonstrate that PRISM achieves state-of-the-art fidelity in noisy depth synthesis. Furthermore, downstream robotic experiments show that PRISM facilitates a \textbf{92.1\%} average success rate in the real world, marking a significant improvement over monolithic baselines. Our project page is available at: \resizebox{\linewidth}{!}{\href{https://shawnleung-sii.github.io/prism-icml2026/}{https://shawnleung-sii.github.io/prism-icml2026/}.}
authors: Xiujian Liang, Jiacheng Liu, Mingyang Sun, Qichen He, Anda Cheng, Cewu Lu, Jianhua Sun
bullets: Addresses the sim-to-real gap caused by heterogeneous real-world depth-sensing noise.
Separates noise into sensing invalidation and measurement inaccuracy for tailored modeling.
Uses 3D Visual Foundation Model features as spatial-semantic priors in a tripartite framework.
Introduces Hierarchical Positive-Prioritized Supervision to detect sparse invalid regions and preserve hard positives.
Reports state-of-the-art noisy-depth fidelity and a 92.1% average real-world robotic success rate.
papers.selection_reason: Physics-grounded depth noise synthesis for sim-to-real robotic perception is a meaningful 3D vision contribution.
papers.title: PRISM: Learning Realistic Depth via Physics-Grounded Noise Disentanglement with Semantic-Geometric Collaboration
papers.tldr: PRISM synthesizes realistic depth noise by physically disentangling sensing invalidation from measurement inaccuracy and combining this modeling with semantic-geometric reasoning.

papers.abstract: 3D semantic occupancy prediction estimates voxel-wise occupancy and semantic labels throughout a scene. Our experiments reveal that conventional sparse transposed-convolution upsampling yields poorly differentiated voxel responses and that successive decoder layers discard previously correct semantic predictions. To address these issues, we present Feature-Diverse Upsampling and Memory-Aware Decoding for 3D Occupancy Prediction (FM-Occ), comprising two components. First, 3D Sparse Subvoxel Shuffle (3S) mitigates feature homogenization by constructing candidate child features in the channel dimension, jointly transforming and normalizing them, and then rearranging them onto a finer sparse grid with explicit feature-coordinate correspondence. Second, Entropy-Regulated Layer-wise Memory (ER-LM) retains semantic information across decoder layers by maintaining a layer-wise memory for each query through gated recurrent updates and using prediction entropy to regulate the historical information propagated to the next layer. During training, a class-weighted entropy loss Lcwe provides label-guided regularization for matched semantic queries. On SemanticKITTI, 3S increases the spatial coefficient of variation of normalized voxel-wise root-mean-square (RMS) responses from 0.41% to 4.03%, while ER-LM reduces semantic degradation and improves error correction across decoder layers. The combined FM-Occ improves mIoU from 12.16% to 12.73% with negligible memory overhead. ER-LM further improves mIoU in the BEV-based DISC framework from 16.78% to 17.17%, supporting its applicability across 3D voxel-based and BEV-based architectures.
authors: Yujia Zhai (Great Bay University), Guoming Huang (Great Bay University), Zhuanghuai Wang (Great Bay University), Bangquan Xie (Great Bay University)
bullets: Addresses feature homogenization from sparse transposed-convolution upsampling and semantic degradation during decoding.
Introduces 3D Sparse Subvoxel Shuffle (3S), which generates and rearranges candidate child features onto a finer sparse grid.
Introduces Entropy-Regulated Layer-wise Memory (ER-LM), using gated memory and prediction entropy to retain and regulate historical semantic information.
On SemanticKITTI, FM-Occ raises mIoU from 12.16% to 12.73% with negligible memory overhead; ER-LM also improves DISC from 16.78% to 17.17%.
Scope: evaluated across voxel-based and BEV-based 3D occupancy architectures.
papers.selection_reason: 3D occupancy prediction with memory-aware decoding, relevant to 3D perception and robot navigation architectures.
papers.title: FM-Occ: Feature-Diverse Upsampling and Memory-Aware Decoding for 3D Occupancy Prediction
papers.tldr: FM-Occ improves 3D semantic occupancy prediction by diversifying sparse upsampling features and preserving semantic information across decoder layers.

papers.abstract: Robots deployed in human-centered environments need maps that support both geometric navigation and open-vocabulary semantic queries beyond a fixed label set. A key challenge is enriching such maps with semantic information without relying on manually annotated segmentation masks or closed-set semantic categories. Existing geometry-driven active mapping maximizes coverage but treats semantics as a passive by-product of the collected trajectory, whereas active semantic mapping typically depends on supervised semantic segmentation. We present AOV-GS, an active 3D Gaussian mapping system that guides exploration using frozen foundation models. During coarse exploration, AOV-GS re-ranks geometrically promising candidate views according to CLIP mask-embedding novelty computed from SAM instance segmentation, biasing exploration toward semantically informative regions. Frozen SAM and CLIP provide instance masks and language-aligned embeddings throughout mapping, while a lightweight scene-specific language field is fitted offline directly to the collected CLIP embeddings rather than manually annotated masks, enabling open-vocabulary text-query segmentation on novel views. In a controlled comparison using the same SAM-CLIP perception stack, AOV-GS improves average language-field mIoU over geometry-only active planning by 1.3 percentage points on Replica (34.6% on eight scenes) and by 1.8 points on Matterport3D (23.1% on five scenes). With CorrCLIP, AOV-GS reaches 35.6% on Replica, 2.0 points above the matched Geometry-based + CorrCLIP baseline. Novel-view PSNR remains comparable to the geometry-only baseline on both datasets while depth L1 improves on Replica. Code is available at https://github.com/OptimusFaber/AOV-GS.
authors: Rodion Shkokov, Tatiana Zemskova, Dmitry Yudin
bullets: Targets robot maps that support both geometric navigation and language-based semantic queries beyond fixed label sets.
Re-ranks candidate views using CLIP embedding novelty from SAM instance masks, complementing geometry-driven exploration.
Fits a lightweight scene-specific language field directly to frozen SAM-CLIP embeddings for text-query segmentation on novel views.
Improves language-field mIoU over matched geometry-only planning by 1.3 points on Replica and 1.8 points on Matterport3D.
Maintains comparable novel-view PSNR and improves depth L1 on Replica; evaluation covers eight Replica and five Matterport3D scenes.
papers.selection_reason: Active open-vocabulary semantic mapping using 3D Gaussian Splatting, directly relevant to embodied AI navigation and 3D foundation models.
papers.title: AOV-GS: Active Open-Vocabulary Semantic Mapping with 3D Gaussian Splatting
papers.tldr: AOV-GS actively explores environments for semantically informative views, enabling open-vocabulary 3D Gaussian maps without manual segmentation annotations.

papers.abstract: As-built BIM reconstruction from point clouds demands semantic, volumetric, parametric, and editable building components, beyond 2D layouts or planar abstractions. Yet existing scan-to-BIM pipelines often rely on handcrafted rules, heuristic optimization, or manual correction, while learning-based methods fall short of recovering wall thickness, opening geometry, and component-level BIM structure. We introduce CRAB, a BIM-ready cuboid reconstruction framework that encodes walls, doors, windows, beams, and columns as compact architectural cuboids with IFC-compatible semantics and parameters. CRAB bridges point clouds and editable BIM by combining ProposalNet, which predicts coarse component cuboids, with AssemblyNet, a relation-aware Flow Matching model that refines geometry, predicts structural relationships, and enables automatic structural correction and human-guided editing. To address limited cuboid-level supervision, we extend Structured3D with component-wise cuboid annotations and construct cuboid-based procedural scenes. Experiments show CRAB surpasses floor plan and plane-based alternatives in component completeness, geometric accuracy, and generalization. For interior wall thickness estimation, CRAB achieves a mean error of 2.80 cm, with 79.50% of matched walls within 3 cm. The project page is available at https://vcc.tech/research/2026/CRAB.
authors: Haoran Xiong, Jing Wang, Shanshan Pan, Zihao Yan, Minglun Gong, Hui Huang
bullets: Targets scan-to-BIM limitations in recovering wall thickness, openings, and structured building components.
Represents walls, doors, windows, beams, and columns as compact architectural cuboids with semantic and parametric information.
Combines ProposalNet for coarse cuboid prediction with AssemblyNet for relation-aware refinement, structural correction, and human-guided editing.
Extends Structured3D with cuboid annotations and creates procedural cuboid-based scenes to support training.
Reports a 2.80 cm mean error for interior wall thickness, with 79.50% of matched walls estimated within 3 cm.
papers.selection_reason: Learning-based point-cloud to BIM cuboid reconstruction with relation-aware flow matching; directly relevant to 3D scene perception.
papers.title: CRAB: Cuboid-based Representation for As-built BIM from Point Clouds
papers.tldr: CRAB reconstructs editable, IFC-compatible BIM components from point clouds using cuboid proposals and relation-aware geometric refinement.

papers.abstract: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) excel at 2D recognition but often fail to maintain consistent 3D relations across sparse viewpoints, leading to spatial hallucinations under occlusion and perspective changes. Existing methods commonly fuse all frames with dense geometry, incurring substantial computation and context overhead while encouraging blind reliance on imperfect estimators. We present Think-Capture, a query-conditioned framework that first identifies task-critical objects and then acquires their geometry on demand. A 3D toolkit lifts zero-shot masks into a common coordinate frame, and a Symbolic 3D State Abstraction compresses object and camera states into structured text. Hierarchical Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) trains the VLM on cases in which geometry either helps or misleads, teaching it when to use tool evidence and when to fall back on visual cues. Think-Capture-4B reaches 54.4% on MindCube-Tiny (+21.5 points over its backbone), 39.1% on the MMSI-Bench positional subset (+7.9), and 42.8% on ViewSpatial (+5.2). It also remains robust under coordinate and mask perturbations. The full stack fits one 24 GB GPU and serves as an asynchronous high-level reasoner on an Agibot G1. Our code is available at https://github.com/819346675/Think-Capture.
authors: Junjie Wang, Zhihao Yuan, Yunhan Tang, Sheng Xu, Jiaqi Mao, Xiaoyu Ye, Yueru Luo, Xu Yan, Chun-Mei Feng, Zhen Li
bullets: Targets spatial hallucinations caused by occlusion, perspective changes, and sparse viewpoints.
Identifies task-critical objects, lifts their zero-shot masks into a shared 3D frame, and compresses geometry into structured text.
Uses hierarchical GRPO to teach the VLM when to trust geometric tools and when to rely on visual evidence.
Think-Capture-4B improves over its backbone by 21.5, 7.9, and 5.2 points on MindCube-Tiny, MMSI-Bench positional, and ViewSpatial, respectively.
The system remains robust to coordinate and mask perturbations, fits on one 24 GB GPU, and runs as an asynchronous reasoner on an Agibot G1.
papers.selection_reason: Query-conditioned active 3D geometry acquisition for VLM spatial reasoning; strongly fits spatial intelligence and 3D-aware multimodal modeling.
papers.title: Think-Capture: Active 3D Geometry Acquisition for Spatial Reasoning in Vision-Language Models
papers.tldr: Think-Capture improves VLM spatial reasoning by selectively acquiring and symbolically representing 3D geometry when it is useful, rather than densely processing every view.

papers.abstract: Recovering dynamic 3D scene geometry, appearance, and the physical motion states that govern scene evolution from multi-view videos is important yet challenging. A key difficulty is that appearance can be deceptive. Under rendering supervision alone, a model may fit the observed images by changing color or opacity to compensate for inaccurate deformation, rather than recovering the true evolving geometry and motion. This issue is especially severe in scenes with fast or locally complex motion, where inaccurate trajectories can still produce plausible images over the observed frames, but lead to unreliable reconstruction and discontinuous future prediction. In this paper, we propose PhyMo, a framework for learning evolving dynamics from multi-view videos. We introduce a Motion-Aware Trajectory Representation that drives the model to recover accurate motion from deformation, rather than relying on appearance shortcuts to explain observed motion. On top of this, we propose a Continuous Motion Evolution module with bidirectional kinematic continuity constraint to promote temporally consistent evolution of displacement, velocity, and acceleration. Together, these designs yield geometrically faithful interpolation and continuous motion extrapolation. Experiments on four dynamic scene benchmarks demonstrate state-of-the-art performance.
authors: Shangjia Liu, Jinxi Li, Siyuan Zhou, Bo Yang, Bing Wang
bullets: Addresses inaccurate geometry and motion recovery when rendering supervision lets appearance compensate for deformation errors.
Uses a Motion-Aware Trajectory Representation to learn motion directly from deformation.
Adds Continuous Motion Evolution with bidirectional continuity constraints on displacement, velocity, and acceleration.
Produces geometrically faithful interpolation and continuous motion extrapolation.
Achieves state-of-the-art performance across four dynamic-scene benchmarks.
papers.selection_reason: Learns physical dynamics and continuous future motion from multi-view video, fitting video world models and 3D dynamic scene recovery.
papers.title: PhyMo: Learning Physical Dynamics with Accurate and Continuous Motion from Multi-View Videos
papers.tldr: PhyMo learns physically faithful, continuous 3D motion from multi-view videos by preventing appearance-based shortcuts and enforcing kinematic consistency.

papers.abstract: Neural Radiance Fields (NeRF) synthesize photorealistic novel views from dense image collections, but degrade sharply when few views are available. We attribute a specific, measurable defect to the objective itself: the rendering loss is a sum over independent rays and contains no term comparing densities that different rays assign to the same region of space, so nearby 3D points can settle on contradictory densities while every training pixel is reproduced correctly. We make this quantity explicit by measuring cross-ray density disagreement directly during training, and show that it stays high in vanilla NeRF, falls only incidentally under frequency-based regularization, and moves together with held-out quality in the sparse regime. We then close the gap with DriftNeRF, a drop-in regularizer that instantiates the drifting-field template on density samples: a masked exponential kernel aggregates densities from nearby points on other rays into a stop-gradient consensus target, and the resulting drifting field penalizes unsupported disagreement while leaving agreed-upon boundaries intact. The regularizer reads only sampled positions, ray identifiers, and predicted densities, so it requires no pretrained model, external geometry, or additional images, and transfers across field parameterizations. On NeRF-Synthetic it reduces residual disagreement by an order of magnitude, and across NeRF-Synthetic, DTU, and LLFF it improves 3-view PSNR over the strongest MLP-NeRF baseline by 0.42-0.65 dB and remains competitive with sparse-view Gaussian pipelines under a matched protocol without their depth, flow, or covisibility preprocessing.
authors: Juntang Wang, Yihan Wang, Sheng'en Li, Hao Wu, Dongmian Zou, Shixin Xu
bullets: Identifies cross-ray density disagreement as a key sparse-view NeRF failure mode: independent ray losses can fit pixels while producing contradictory 3D densities.
Measures this disagreement during training and finds it remains high in vanilla NeRF and correlates with held-out quality.
Uses a drop-in masked-kernel regularizer that builds a stop-gradient consensus from nearby samples on other rays.
Requires only sampled positions, ray IDs, and predicted densities, with no extra images, pretrained models, or external geometry.
Reports order-of-magnitude lower residual disagreement and 0.42–0.65 dB higher 3-view PSNR than the strongest MLP-NeRF baseline across several benchmarks.
papers.selection_reason: Regularizer addressing cross-ray density drifting in sparse-view NeRF, directly relevant to 3D vision.
papers.title: DriftNeRF: Cross-Ray Density Drifting for Sparse-View Neural Radiance Fields
papers.tldr: DriftNeRF improves sparse-view NeRF rendering by regularizing inconsistent densities assigned to the same 3D regions across rays.

papers.abstract: One-shot landmark localization in volume scans with varying fields of view (FOVs) is challenging. While existing self-supervised learning methods have shown promising performance, they rely on contrastive learning built upon augmented views of the same image, which inherently limits their generalization in cross-modality scenarios. This motivates research on cross-modality embedding learning using paired multi-modality images. However, existing methods suffer from not only limited training data, but also the requirement of multi-stage iterative training. To address these limitations, we propose UNIVERS, an end-to-end trainable framework that learns UNIversal Voxel-wise Embedding via Randomized Synthesis. Our framework leverages diverse pseudo-data synthesized from organ shape templates, with randomization applied to semantic layout, visual appearance, FOV, and spatial pose. Coupled with cross-domain discriminative voxel-wise contrastive learning, this domain randomization strategy forces the network to disregard domain-specific biases and learn features that are robust against variations in imaging contrast, resolution, and spatial context. Consequently, the trained model enables one-shot landmark localization in multi-modality volume scans with arbitrary FOVs. In this study, the efficacy of the proposed method is demonstrated by applying it to the task of localizing the adrenal glands, which are paired, small, and irregular endocrine organs. In particular, comprehensive experiments are conducted on three challenging adrenal gland datasets. The experimental results demonstrate that UNIVERS consistently outperforms the state-of-the-art (SOTA) one-shot landmark localization approaches, with particularly prominent advantages in cross-modality scenarios. The source code is publicly available at https://github.com/Kendra9999/UNIVERS.
authors: Derong Yu, Qingsong Zhao, Yanbing Yue, Yikai Li, Zhi Zhang, Guoyan Zheng
bullets: Targets cross-modality one-shot landmark localization in volume scans with varying or arbitrary FOVs.
Uses an end-to-end framework combining randomized synthesis of pseudo-data with cross-domain discriminative voxel-wise contrastive learning.
Randomizes organ layouts, appearance, FOV, and pose to reduce domain-specific biases and improve robustness to contrast, resolution, and spatial-context changes.
Evaluated on adrenal-gland localization across three challenging datasets, where it consistently outperforms existing state-of-the-art methods, especially across modalities.
Scope demonstrated on paired, small, irregular adrenal glands; source code is publicly available.
papers.selection_reason: Introduces UNIVERS, a framework for learning generalizable voxel-wise embeddings in 3D medical scans via randomized synthesis and cross-domain contrastive learning.
papers.title: UNIVERS: Learning UNIversal Voxel-wise Embedding via Randomized Synthesis for generalizable one-shot landmark localization
papers.tldr: UNIVERS enables robust one-shot landmark localization across modalities and arbitrary fields of view by learning voxel embeddings from heavily randomized synthetic data.

papers.abstract: Abdominal organ segmentation is essential in modern medical applications. While existing deep learning approaches demonstrate promising performance, their heavy reliance on large-scale image data raises concerns over generalization capability and privacy risks. This motivates the development of generalizable segmentation training paradigms based on domain-randomized image synthesis, facilitating generalization across unseen real image domains. However, existing paradigms either suffer from limited segmentation performance when applied to abdominal organs, or require dataset-specific finetuning. To address these limitations, we propose ReSeg, a novel two-stage retraining-free framework for domain-agnostic zero-shot abdominal organ segmentation. At the first stage, our organ-agnostic synthetic data-driven pretraining approach exploits semantically and visually diverse synthetic images generated by a dedicated data engine to optimize a Generalizable Semantic Representation Network (GSRNet). The network is thereby capable of learning semantic features robust against variations in anatomical structure, imaging contrast, resolution and spatial context, which provide universal representation capabilities that serve as a foundation for segmentation learning. Subsequently, in the second stage, we continue to train an Organ-specific Encoder-decoder Segmentation Network (OESNet), whose encoder is initialized with the pretrained weights. This training process is facilitated by another dedicated data engine, which generates diversified visual images while strictly retaining the inherent spatial layout of abdominal organs. Comprehensive evaluation on seven abdominal organ segmentation datasets across three different modalities including CT, MRI, and PET demonstrates that ReSeg consistently outperforms existing state-of-the-art (SOTA) methods while eliminating the need for real training images.
bullets: Addresses limited cross-domain generalization, privacy concerns, and the need for dataset-specific fine-tuning in abdominal organ segmentation.
Uses a two-stage framework: organ-agnostic synthetic pretraining of GSRNet, followed by organ-specific OESNet training initialized from the learned encoder.
Employs dedicated data engines to generate visually diverse synthetic images while preserving organ layouts and semantic structure.
Learns representations robust to anatomical, contrast, resolution, and spatial-context variations.
Evaluation across seven datasets and three imaging modalities shows consistent improvement over existing state-of-the-art methods without real training images.
papers.selection_reason: Proposes a generalizable pretraining framework (ReSeg) for 3D medical image segmentation using domain-randomized synthesis and semantic representation learning.
papers.title: ReSeg: Retraining-free segmentation of abdominal organs via generalizable semantic representation learning
papers.tldr: ReSeg enables retraining-free, zero-shot abdominal organ segmentation across unseen CT, MRI, and PET domains using synthetic-data-driven semantic representation learning.

papers.abstract: True whole-body medical imaging captures a patient from head to toe and provides comprehensive anatomical and/or functional information. This coverage enables reconstruction of the external body surface, yielding patient body models. However, scanner geometry (e.g., bore diameter), patient characteristics, and positioning can leave body regions missing (e.g., lateral arms/torso, hands, forearms, elbows), producing incomplete patient body models. Such incompleteness limits downstream medical analyses, including derivation of body-habitus metrics (BHMs), such as body volume and surface area, for injected radiotracer activity regimens, cardiometabolic risk assessment, and computational anatomical modeling for medical imaging simulation and radiation dosimetry. We present the Medical Body model Optimization-based Estimator (MedBOE), an automated, training-free framework for estimating complete patient body models from whole-body images with missing body regions. Our innovation is to leverage the Skinned Multi-Person Linear (SMPL) template, a parametric body mesh representing a broad range of body shapes and poses, in medical imaging. MedBOE aligns the SMPL template to the incomplete patient body models via attribute-guided optimization and estimates missing body regions through geometrically and volumetrically constrained deformation. We evaluated MedBOE using two public datasets: AutoPET (91 whole-body PET-CT images) and Human Implicit Tissues (HIT; 40 whole-body segmentations from MRI images). MedBOE achieved the best overall volumetric and geometric performance among evaluated methods. BHMs derived from MedBOE were within 2% error, suggesting low percentage errors for downstream analyses. MedBOE offers an automated, training-free method for estimating complete patient body models from whole-body images with missing body regions.
authors: Hoijoon Jung, Yuhao Wei, Mingxiao Tu, Younhyun Jung, Michael Fulham, Jinman Kim
bullets: Addresses incomplete body models caused by scanner geometry, patient characteristics, and positioning.
Aligns a parametric SMPL body template to observed anatomy using attribute-guided optimization.
Deforms the template under geometric and volumetric constraints to estimate missing regions.
Evaluated on AutoPET PET-CT and HIT MRI segmentation datasets, achieving the best overall reported geometric and volumetric performance.
Derived body-habitus metrics were within 2% error, supporting downstream medical analyses.
papers.selection_reason: Whole-body 3D patient model estimation from medical images; fits 3D perception and geometry.
papers.title: MedBOE: Optimization-Based Estimation of Complete Patient Body Models from Whole-Body Medical Imaging
papers.tldr: MedBOE uses optimization-guided SMPL body meshes to reconstruct missing regions in whole-body medical-image-derived patient models without training.

papers.abstract: Accurate 6-DoF object pose tracking is essential for robotic interaction, yet conventional monocular pipelines frequently suffer from catastrophic divergence under rapid object motion. We present RoPT, a robust tracking framework engineered to overcome this limitation by unifying visual perception, temporal kinematics, and global re-localization into a tightly coupled closed loop. Unlike existing open-loop trackers, RoPT delivers three critical capabilities that fundamentally alter system resilience. First, the visual perception component tracks object masks to robustly handle partial and severe occlusions. Second, a kinematic factor graph regularizes frame-to-frame updates, forecasts forward pose predictions, and drives a parallel multi-hypothesis verification scheme to bypass local minima. Finally, an active re-localization module transforms the pipeline into a closed-loop system, making it failure-aware and capable of deterministic self-recovery. We demonstrate the effectiveness of our framework across challenging benchmarks alongside real-world robotic demonstrations, achieving significantly higher tracking survivability under rapid motion.
authors: Yongqing Liang, Yuzhong Chen, Sihang Li, Junsuk Kim, Chase Kidder, Hui-ping Wang, Yunzhi Xu, Raihan Haque, Yubiao Zhang, Chen Feng
bullets: Targets catastrophic divergence in conventional monocular pose trackers caused by rapid object motion.
Tracks object masks to remain robust under partial and severe occlusions.
Uses a kinematic factor graph for temporal regularization and forward pose prediction.
Employs parallel multi-hypothesis verification to avoid local minima.
Demonstrates higher tracking survivability on challenging benchmarks and in real-world robotic demonstrations.
papers.selection_reason: Robust 6DoF object pose tracking for robotic interaction; relevant to embodied perception and 3D vision.
papers.title: RoPT: Robust 6DoF Object Pose Tracking in Video
papers.tldr: RoPT improves robust 6DoF object pose tracking during rapid motion by combining occlusion-aware perception, kinematic reasoning, multi-hypothesis verification, and active self-relocalization.

papers.abstract: We present Register Anything Model (RAM), a unified model for generalizable 3D point cloud registration that robustly estimates 6-DoF transformations across diverse domains spanning sensors and environments. Existing registration methods are typically tailored to a single domain, with carefully tuned architectures and hyperparameters, and thus degrade markedly when applied to novel domains. We bridge this gap by training a single model on diverse data from indoor, outdoor, and object domains. A central challenge is the severe geometric discrepancy across domains, i.e., differences in scene scale, sensor noise, point density, and structural patterns, which hinders processing with a unified point-based model. To address this, we introduce a geometry-aware normalization strategy that jointly voxelizes and normalizes point clouds into a standardized geometric space, adaptively based on their geometric properties to preserve salient local structures while standardizing resolution. Built on this normalization, RAM follows a hierarchical coarse-to-fine paradigm, and employs an efficient geometric transformer that models local geometric consistency instead of globally over all points. This design mitigates discretization noise introduced by voxelization, and improves computational efficiency. Extensive experiments on 12 benchmarks demonstrate state-of-the-art performance in terms of inlier ratio and registration recall. Notably, our method outperforms the counterparts trained on each separate domain, showing superior generalization capability.
authors: Zheng Qin, Junhua Xi, Yan Huang, Jiahong Lai, Anwen Huang, Qiong Li, Guangda Zhang, Kai Xu
bullets: Targets the poor cross-domain generalization of registration methods tuned to individual sensors or environments.
Jointly voxelizes and normalizes point clouds according to their geometry, standardizing resolution while preserving salient local structures.
Uses a hierarchical coarse-to-fine pipeline with a local geometric transformer for efficient geometric-consistency modeling.
Trained on diverse indoor, outdoor, and object data, RAM achieves state-of-the-art inlier ratio and registration recall across 12 benchmarks.
Outperforms models trained separately for each domain, demonstrating stronger generalization across domains.
papers.selection_reason: Unified generalizable 3D point cloud registration across domains fits 3D vision and generalist 3D modeling.
papers.title: Register Anything Model for Generalizable and Robust Point Cloud Registration
papers.tldr: RAM is a unified point-cloud registration model that uses geometry-aware normalization and efficient hierarchical matching to generalize robustly across diverse 3D domains.

papers.abstract: Reference-based 3D scene stylization transfers the appearance of a reference image onto a reconstructed 3D scene while preserving scene geometry. Recent methods perform this transfer by optimizing the appearance representation of neural scene models including Neural Radiance Fields (NeRF) and 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS). These methods optimize an RGB appearance representation, in which a single per-point colour combines the effects of material reflectance, environment illumination, together with the shading it produces, and the viewing direction. When stylization modifies this combined colour, the illumination effects present during stylization are baked into the stored appearance, so the stylized scene cannot be rendered under different illumination. To address this limitation, we present RxGS, a relightable 3D scene stylization framework built on a Bidirectional Reflectance Distribution Function (BRDF)-aware 3D Gaussian representation. Rather than modifying a per-point RGB colour, RxGS optimizes only the diffuse albedo field recovered by inverse rendering, while leaving roughness, metallicity, surface normals, and the estimated environment lighting unchanged. As a result, the stylized scene keeps all the components a physically-based renderer needs other than the edited albedo, and can therefore still be relit. RxGS optimizes the albedo field using a nearest-neighbour feature matching loss together with a spatial smoothness prior over Gaussian centres. We evaluate the method using a Geometry Consistency Cost (GCC) based on optical-flow warping error. RxGS achieves the lowest GCC on all evaluated NeRF-Synthetic scenes and remains competitive on real-captured scenes, while additionally supporting relightable stylization, which existing reference-based 3D scene stylization methods do not provide.
bullets: Existing methods combine material, lighting, shading, and view effects into RGB, preventing relighting after stylization.
RxGS uses a BRDF-aware 3D Gaussian representation and keeps roughness, metallicity, normals, and estimated environment lighting unchanged.
Albedo optimization combines nearest-neighbour feature matching with a spatial smoothness prior over Gaussian centres.
It achieves the lowest geometry-consistency cost on all evaluated NeRF-Synthetic scenes and remains competitive on real-captured scenes.
The abstract does not specify limitations beyond performance variation between synthetic and real-captured scenes.
papers.selection_reason: Relightable 3D scene stylization via BRDF-aware Gaussian splatting; fits 3D scene generation though not foundation-model-focused.
papers.title: RxGS: Relightable Gaussian Stylization via BRDF Decomposition
papers.tldr: RxGS enables reference-based 3D scene stylization that preserves geometry and remains relightable by editing only the diffuse albedo instead of baked RGB appearance.

papers.abstract: Video generation models can now depict remarkably realistic motion. Yet it is unclear how to use this motion beyond pixels: to animate a specific 3D asset and replay the animation in its 3D scene. For instance, a video model can show a monkey jumping over a crossbar, but it cannot return that jump as replayable 3D motion placed in the 3D scene. Here we present a model that directly co-generates the video and 3D motion for any supplied rig, along with a camera that registers this motion to the scene. Prior video-motion models either handle only human skeletons, often adding billions of parameters, or triangulate 3D motion from generated 2D pose maps. We instead keep 3D motion in a separate model that supports arbitrary skeletons, and connect it to a pretrained video model through a small set of cross-attention layers. This separation lets the motion model first learn how skeletons move from motion-only data, which is easier to obtain and augment than paired video. Additionally, our model learns to locate each joint in the video frames, which lets us recover the camera and place the 3D motion in the scene. To train across many skeletons, we use a generative video editor to place animated 3D assets in scenes suited to their actions, curating the edits so their known motion remains valid. Together with human and robot video, this yields nearly 200K training pairs. Our evaluations demonstrate that our model animates diverse rigs from text more faithfully than video-first pipelines, and its motion responds to the surrounding scene. It also turns video into rig motion, rig motion into video, and enables keyframe-based control of the 3D motion. Videos and additional results are available on our project page: https://research.nvidia.com/labs/par/projects/jca/.
authors: Noam Rotstein, Yoad Tewel, Chen Tessler, Haggai Maron, Gal Chechik, Or Litany, Yoni Kasten, Yuval Atzmon
bullets: Addresses the gap between realistic video generation and usable 3D animation for specific assets.
Separates an arbitrary-skeleton 3D motion model from a pretrained video model, linking them with lightweight cross-attention.
Predicts joint locations in video to recover the camera and register 3D motion in the scene.
Uses curated synthetic edits plus human and robot video to create nearly 200K training pairs.
Supports text-to-motion/video, video-to-rig motion, rig-motion-to-video, and keyframe control; evaluations report more faithful, scene-responsive animation than video-first pipelines.
papers.selection_reason: Co-generates 3D motion and video for arbitrary rigs from human/robot video; transferable to embodied animation and 3D motion generation.
papers.title: Joints, Camera, Action! Co-Generating 3D Motion and Video for Arbitrary Rigs
papers.tldr: Joints, Camera, Action! co-generates scene-aware video, camera motion, and replayable 3D motion for arbitrary rigs from text or video.

papers.abstract: Simulation is a powerful tool for robotics, but building diverse, simulation-ready scenes at scale remains difficult. Reconstructing scenes from single images is a promising alternative, but visual similarity alone is insufficient: objects must also be recovered, accurately placed, and physically grounded. Existing methods that rely on post-hoc physics settling often misplace objects, producing scenes that look correct but behave poorly under manipulation. We present SceneRig, an agentic system that turns a single image into an editable, simulation-ready scene. SceneRig combines geometric, visual, and physical tools to reconstruct a faithful 3D scene. An agent then performs edit-and-validate loops inside a physics simulator to achieve physical stability. Across diverse inputs, SceneRig improves instance segmentation, object-centric appearance, and 3D placement while keeping the reconstructed scenes physically stable. Furthermore, SceneRig is effective for downstream robotics: its scenes predict real-robot policy outcomes more accurately than the baseline method and more reliably support replay of recorded manipulations without trajectory adaptation.
authors: Rundong Luo, Yunong Liu, Di Cao, Matthew Tancik, Shyamal Buch, Colton Stearns, Wenqi Xian
bullets: Addresses the gap between visually plausible reconstruction and physically correct object placement.
Combines geometric, visual, and physical tools with agent-driven edit-and-validate loops in a physics simulator.
Improves instance segmentation, object-centric appearance, and 3D placement across diverse inputs.
Produces physically stable scenes that better predict real-robot policy outcomes than the baseline.
Supports more reliable replay of recorded manipulations without trajectory adaptation.
papers.selection_reason: Agentic system for 3D scene reconstruction from single images with physical grounding, directly applicable to simulation and downstream robotics tasks.
papers.title: SceneRig: An Agentic System for Simulation-Ready 3D Scene Reconstruction from Single Images
papers.tldr: SceneRig reconstructs editable, physically stable 3D scenes from single images for more reliable simulation and robot-policy evaluation.

papers.abstract: Collaborative perception enables agents to retrieve the scene semantics and geometry beyond the field of view of any individual agent. This broader scene understanding enhances transportation safety and improves efficiency in multi-robot systems. However, existing collaborative semantic occupancy methods rely on dense 3D voxel annotations and are limited to recognizing objects within a predefined set of semantic classes. To overcome these limitations, we present CoGaussian, an open-vocabulary Gaussian-based collaborative semantic occupancy prediction framework. CoGaussian represents a scene as a set of foundation model-aligned sparse 3D Gaussians, which serve as a compact representation for communicating and fusing geometric and semantic information across multiple agents. On the Semantic-OPV2V benchmark, our method outperforms existing open-vocabulary single-agent approaches, highlighting the effectiveness of open-vocabulary collaborative scene understanding.
authors: Om Shivam Verma, Shaya Farahmand, Lingjun Zhao, Lu Gan
bullets: Addresses the limits of existing collaborative semantic occupancy methods, which require dense 3D voxel annotations and fixed semantic classes.
Represents scenes with sparse 3D Gaussians aligned to foundation models.
Uses Gaussians to communicate and fuse geometric and semantic information across agents.
Evaluated on Semantic-OPV2V, where it outperforms existing open-vocabulary single-agent methods.
Targets broader scene understanding for transportation safety and multi-robot efficiency.
papers.selection_reason: Open-vocabulary collaborative 3D scene understanding with foundation-aligned 3D Gaussians; fits spatial intelligence and 3D scene understanding.
papers.title: CoGaussian: Open-Vocabulary Gaussian-based Collaborative 3D Scene Understanding
papers.tldr: CoGaussian enables multiple agents to collaboratively understand 3D scenes with open-vocabulary semantics using compact, foundation-model-aligned Gaussian representations.

papers.abstract: Video generation and feed-forward 3D reconstruction typically use separate representations, requiring RGB decoding and visual re-encoding to recover geometry from generated latents. We propose Latent Bridge, which connects video generative latent spaces with geometric feature spaces to directly predict 3D geometry from video latents. We develop representation-specific bridges for Wan2.1 and V-RAE, enabling feed-forward prediction of cameras, depth, and 3D point clouds without the intermediate RGB pathway. Each bridge is trained on RGB videos through feature distillation, while the video encoder and geometry model remain frozen. Training requires neither ground-truth geometry nor execution of the downstream geometric aggregator or prediction heads. At inference, the same video latents support both RGB decoding and geometry prediction. The same trained bridge can be reused for image-to-video and text-to-video generation within the same video latent space, without bridge retraining. Experiments on Co3Dv2 and WildRGB-D demonstrate competitive geometric reconstruction quality, efficient end-to-end generation and reconstruction, and faster latent-to-geometry decoding, highlighting latent alignment as a practical and reusable interface between video generation and 3D reconstruction. Our code is available at: https://github.com/hustvl/Latent-Bridge.
authors: Shuai Zhang, Zhanpeng Ouyang, Zhengqing Chen, Ruohong Mei, Shaoyu Chen, Weiqiang Ren, Hui Sun, Qian Zhang, Wenyu Liu, Xinggang Wang
bullets: Addresses the inefficiency of recovering geometry from generated video latents through an intermediate RGB pathway.
Learns representation-specific bridges for Wan2.1 and V-RAE to predict cameras, depth, and 3D point clouds.
Uses feature distillation on RGB videos while freezing the video encoder and geometry model; no ground-truth geometry is required.
The same bridge supports image-to-video and text-to-video generation within a latent space without retraining.
Experiments on Co3Dv2 and WildRGB-D show competitive reconstruction, efficient generation–reconstruction, and faster latent-to-geometry decoding.
papers.selection_reason: Bridges video generative latents directly to 3D geometry prediction; relevant to 3D vision and video-model interfaces.
papers.title: Latent Bridge: From Video Latents to 3D Geometry via Feature Alignment
papers.tldr: Latent Bridge directly converts video-generation latents into 3D geometry, avoiding RGB decoding and re-encoding while retaining competitive reconstruction quality and faster decoding.

papers.abstract: Deep learning models have become essential tools in medical imaging, yet training them end-to-end for diverse tasks remains challenging due to limited labeled data and computational constraints. To address this, we introduce Brain2Vec, a foundation model pre-trained on 74,425 T1-weighted Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) scans pooled from multiple studies. Brain2Vec can serve both as a weight initialization backbone for fine-tuning downstream tasks and as a standalone feature extractor. We evaluated Brain2Vec in three tasks: downstream predictive performance, convergence speed, and embedding quality. Using Brain2Vec's pretrained weights as initialization and fine-tuning on labeled data for a brain age prediction task, results demonstrate improved final accuracy and faster convergence compared to random initialization. Additionally, its frozen embeddings outperform anatomically defined volumetric features on four of five downstream classification tasks and perform competitively with a state-of-the-art foundation model pre-trained on substantially more data. Lastly, we show that Brain2Vec encodes information primarily from a spatially localized and neuroanatomically meaningful set of brain regions, and that manipulating a subset of latent features produces monotonic, region-specific effects on the reconstructed anatomy. Brain2Vec code and trained models are available as an open-source package on https://github.com/CBICA/Brain2Vec. Users can apply Brain2Vec locally by installing the package, or directly through the NiChart cloud platform https://cloud.neuroimagingchart.com, where Brain2Vec features can be derived without requiring local installation or specialized infrastructure.
authors: Spiros Maggioros, Guray Erus, Gareth Harman, George Aidinis, Alexander Getka, Aristeidis Sotiras, Christos Davatzikos
bullets: Pre-trained on 74,425 T1-weighted MRI scans pooled from multiple studies.
Supports both weight initialization for downstream fine-tuning and standalone feature extraction.
Improved brain-age prediction accuracy and convergence speed relative to random initialization.
Frozen embeddings outperformed anatomical volumetric features on four of five classification tasks and competed with a larger-data foundation model.
Latent features capture spatially localized, neuroanatomically meaningful information with region-specific effects on reconstructed anatomy.
papers.selection_reason: Self-supervised 3D foundation model for brain MRI; fits 3D foundation models.
papers.title: Brain2Vec: A Self-Supervised 3D Foundation Model for Structural Brain MRI
papers.tldr: Brain2Vec is a self-supervised 3D foundation model for structural brain MRI that improves fine-tuning efficiency and provides informative, neuroanatomically meaningful embeddings.

papers.abstract: Reconstructing dynamic 3D scenes from monocular video requires inferring motion from noisy and intermittently visible observations. Long-range tracks provide valuable geometric constraints, but integrating their fragmented temporal coverage into shared, continuous motion remains challenging. We introduce \textbf{RayCo4D}, a ray-conditioned continuous motion model for monocular 4D reconstruction that explicitly separates visual measurements from latent 3D motion states. Each track is associated with a reference-time 3D query constrained to its camera ray, and its image and depth observations constrain shared latent motion nodes through local many-to-many associations. Each node maintains an $\mathrm{SE}(3)$ pose and body-frame velocity at sparse support times. A white-noise-on-acceleration process prior couples neighboring states and defines continuous-time interpolation, allowing observations across visibility intervals to jointly constrain the same latent state sequence.The inferred shared motion is transferred to Gaussian primitives through dual-quaternion blending, while reference-anchored local $\mathrm{SE}(3)$ residuals capture fine-scale non-rigid deformation beyond the shared scaffold. Experiments on diverse monocular dynamic scenes show that RayCo4D achieves competitive novel-view synthesis quality, improves structural and temporal consistency under rapid motion and incomplete tracks, and supports continuous-time rendering.
authors: Yuanxiang Ni, Xianliang Huang, Ruihan Hou, Feng Xie, Hao Zhang
bullets: Addresses noisy, intermittently visible observations and fragmented long-range tracks in monocular dynamic reconstruction.
Uses camera-ray-constrained reference-time 3D queries and many-to-many associations to connect observations to shared latent motion nodes.
Models each node with an SE(3) pose and body-frame velocity, coupled by a white-noise-on-acceleration prior for continuous-time interpolation.
Transfers shared motion to Gaussian primitives via dual-quaternion blending, with local SE(3) residuals for fine non-rigid deformation.
Reports competitive novel-view synthesis and improved structural and temporal consistency under rapid motion and incomplete tracks, with continuous-time rendering support.
papers.selection_reason: Monocular 4D dynamic scene reconstruction with a continuous motion model; fits 3D vision perception and reconstruction.
papers.title: RayCo4D: Ray-Conditioned Continuous Motion Model for Monocular 4D Dynamic Reconstruction
papers.tldr: RayCo4D reconstructs monocular dynamic 4D scenes by combining ray-constrained 3D queries with continuous, shared latent motion and local deformation modeling.

papers.abstract: Geometric Relative Positional Encoding has become the primary mechanism for injecting spatial inductive biases into multi-view transformers. Existing designs condition attention on camera-level frustums or ray-marched depth, associating cross-view tokens through the sensor geometry. Such sensor-centric formulations, however, describe only where a token is observed from, leaving the rich surface geometry of the scene region depicted by the token. In this paper, we advocate a shift toward surface-aware positional encoding that explicitly grounds patch tokens in the geometry of physical surfaces. We introduce HRoPE, which represents the local geometry of each patch as a slanted 3D plane, following the slanted support-window assumption of classical multi-view stereo. We inject token-level, plane-induced homographies into attention as relative transformations. This equips the transformer with a geometric prior for rectifying perspective distortions and aligning patch features across viewpoints. Our encoding requires no ground-truth geometry: the plane parameters can be predicted end-to-end under a view-synthesis objective alone, or derived from foundation models. Extensive experiments on RealEstate10K, CO3Dv2, and DL3DV show that our best variant of HRoPE consistently outperforms the evaluated geometric positional encodings for novel view synthesis. Extensive ablations and analysis show the effectiveness of the proposed encoding. Please refer to our project page at: https://gaohchen.github.io/HRoPE
authors: Huachen Gao, Yang Yang, Xiaoqian Liang, Xingyu Chen, Youjia Zhang, Qi Zhang, Baorui Ma, Anpei Chen, Wei Yang
bullets: Targets the limitation of sensor-centric positional encodings, which model camera rays but not the depicted surface geometry.
Represents each image patch as a locally slanted 3D plane and injects its induced homography as a relative attention transformation.
Plane parameters can be learned end-to-end from view synthesis alone or obtained from foundation models, without ground-truth geometry.
Experiments on RealEstate10K, CO3Dv2, and DL3DV report consistent gains over evaluated geometric positional encodings for novel view synthesis.
Ablations and analysis support the effectiveness of the surface-aware encoding.
papers.selection_reason: Surface-aware geometric positional encoding injecting spatial priors into multi-view transformers, relevant to 3D vision and spatial intelligence.
papers.title: HRoPE: Homography Relative Positional Encoding
papers.tldr: HRoPE improves multi-view transformer geometry by using plane-induced homographies to align patch features across viewpoints.

papers.abstract: Low-cost multi-zone single-photon avalanche diode (SPAD) sensors provide compact time-of-flight measurements but are limited by sparse sampling and unreliable depth estimates near geometric discontinuities. This letter presents a reliability-aware reconstruction framework for V-shaped surfaces using two complementary TMF8821 acquisition configurations. Point-wise reliability is learned from sensor confidence, transient peak amplitude, and peak sharpness, and is incorporated into a graph-based depth optimization. The reconstructed geometry is evaluated by robust two-plane fitting and a perpendicular cross-section. Experiments on 60-degree, 90-degree, and 120-degree targets reduce the mean V-angle error from 11.21 degrees to 9.66 degrees (13.8%). For the representative 90-degree target, the combined point-to-plane RMSE decreases from 14.56 mm to 13.65 mm.
bullets: Addresses unreliable depth estimates near geometric discontinuities in low-cost SPAD time-of-flight sensing.
Combines two TMF8821 acquisition configurations for complementary measurements.
Learns point-wise reliability from sensor confidence, transient peak amplitude, and peak sharpness.
Uses reliability in graph-based depth optimization, evaluated through two-plane fitting and perpendicular cross-sections.
Across 60°, 90°, and 120° targets, mean V-angle error drops from 11.21° to 9.66%; the 90° target’s point-to-plane RMSE falls from 14.56 mm to 13.65 mm.
papers.selection_reason: Reliability-aware depth reconstruction of 3D surfaces from SPAD sensor data, relevant to 3D geometry perception.
papers.title: Reliability-Aware Reconstruction of V-Shaped Surfaces with a Low-Cost Multi-Zone SPAD Sensor
papers.tldr: A reliability-aware graph reconstruction method improves V-shaped surface depth recovery from sparse, noisy multi-zone SPAD measurements.

papers.abstract: This work presents SplatFlux, a feed-forward latent-to-4DGS framework for both video-based 4D reconstruction and conditional 4D generation. Our key observation is that observed videos and conditionally generated content can be represented in the same pretrained video latent space, allowing both tasks to be formulated as latent-to-4DGS decoding. To construct compact and temporally coherent 4D scenes, SplatFlux introduces a static-dynamic decoupled 4D Gaussian representation that explicitly predicts dynamic probabilities for Gaussian primitives. This representation separates static scene structures from moving regions, enabling complete 4D scene construction in a feed-forward manner through static aggregation and dynamic motion interpolation. To learn static-dynamic decomposition and dynamic Gaussian motion without costly annotations, we further develop an auxiliary distillation strategy that provides pseudo dynamic masks and optical-flow cues. Extensive experiments across 3D and 4D reconstruction and generation demonstrate that SplatFlux achieves state-of-the-art performance.
authors: Runmin Zhang, Binglin Ren, Zhu Yu, Fudong Wang, Jiangke Lin, Yichun Shentu, Si-Yuan Cao, Yi Yuan, Hui-Liang Shen
bullets: Unifies observed-video reconstruction and conditional 4D generation through a shared pretrained video latent space.
Uses a static-dynamic decoupled 4D Gaussian representation with dynamic probabilities for each Gaussian primitive.
Builds scenes via static aggregation and dynamic motion interpolation.
