Runs online on a Unitree Go2 with a Jetson Orin NX over a 1.47-km indoor trajectory, achieving 0.141 m endpoint closure error.
papers.selection_reason: Hybrid LiDAR-inertial neural implicit SLAM for real-time onboard navigation; relevant to 3D perception and embodied robot navigation.
papers.title: LIN-SLAM: Lightweight LiDAR--Inertial Neural SLAM for Real-Time Onboard Navigation
papers.tldr: LIN-SLAM combines fast geometric LiDAR–inertial estimation with a lightweight neural implicit backend to deliver accurate, real-time onboard SLAM.

papers.abstract: Point cloud upsampling is essential for 3D applications but remains challenging due to sparse, under-constrained observations. Multi-view images can resolve geometric ambiguity, but existing multi-modal methods do not fully exploit visual cues. We propose ControlFlow3D, a framework that distills knowledge from pretrained foundation models into a lightweight generation network during training, enabling strong performance without multi-view images available at test time. Specifically, our method performs conditional flow matching in a structured latent space defined by a frozen 3D encoder. Multi-view image tokens and 3D latent tokens are jointly clustered into shared prototypes via unsupervised soft KMeans; the resulting prototypes guide the flow trajectory through velocity control and are aligned by a consistency loss that progressively transfers image knowledge into the base network. A Mamba-based geometry decoder then maps latent features to dense coordinates with linear complexity. We also construct ShapeNetPU, a 35K-object multi-modal benchmark that is 31 times larger than prior datasets. Extensive experiments across multiple benchmarks demonstrate the effectiveness of our method and its strong generalization capability.
authors: Yuang Liu, Zhi Zuo, Zhengkai Zhao, Lirui Zhang, Pan Gao, Hao Feng, Zhengzhe Liu
bullets: Addresses geometric ambiguity from sparse point clouds by leveraging multi-view information during training.
Uses conditional flow matching in a structured latent space from a frozen 3D encoder.
Aligns clustered image and 3D latent prototypes to control flow trajectories and transfer visual knowledge.
Employs a Mamba-based decoder to generate dense coordinates with linear complexity.
Introduces ShapeNetPU, a 35K-object multi-modal benchmark, and reports strong cross-benchmark generalization.
papers.selection_reason: Point cloud upsampling via multi-view knowledge distillation and latent flow matching; relevant to 3D perception and generation.
papers.title: ControlFlow3D: Distilling Multi-View Knowledge into Latent Flow Matching for Point Cloud Upsampling
papers.tldr: ControlFlow3D distills multi-view visual knowledge into a lightweight latent flow-matching model for accurate point cloud upsampling without requiring images at test time.

papers.abstract: Real-time mobile volumetric video enables immersive free-viewpoint experiences, but delivering high-quality 3D content under constrained bandwidth and computation remains challenging. Recent 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) systems, such as V$^3$, enable efficient mobile streaming by encoding time-varying Gaussian attributes with commodity video codecs and hardware decoding. However, existing pipelines treat all Gaussians as frame-varying signals, which is poorly suited to full-scene content where large portions remain temporally stable. Our empirical study shows that frame-wise adaptation and video coding of all Gaussians cause quality degradation in complex full-scene content, particularly in temporally stable regions. To address this issue, we propose ResStreamGS, a residual-sensitive dual-stream framework that processes Gaussians according to their temporal behavior. ResStreamGS identifies residual-sensitive primitives through lightweight probe adaptation and reuses stable Gaussians within each Group of Pictures (GOP). Stable Gaussians are transmitted once per GOP, while only residual-sensitive Gaussians remain in the frame-wise hardware-decodable video stream. Experiments on complex full-scene volumetric videos show that ResStreamGS improves post-codec PSNR by 7.51--8.35~dB over a controlled V$^3$-style all-Gaussians baseline, reduces amortized payload by up to 56.5%, and achieves 30.883~FPS on a Qualcomm Snapdragon 778G platform.
authors: Haoran Liu, Di Wu, Wang Luo, Hengyuan Na, Miao Hu, Guocong Quan
bullets: Targets quality degradation and bandwidth/computation inefficiency when all Gaussians are treated as frame-varying.
Uses lightweight probe adaptation to identify residual-sensitive Gaussian primitives.
Transmits stable Gaussians once per GOP and keeps only residual-sensitive Gaussians in the frame-wise hardware-decodable stream.
On complex full-scene videos, improves post-codec PSNR by 7.51–8.35 dB and reduces amortized payload by up to 56.5% versus a controlled V$^3$-style baseline.
Reaches 30.883 FPS on a Qualcomm Snapdragon 778G platform.
papers.selection_reason: Proposes ResStreamGS for efficient mobile volumetric video streaming using 3D Gaussian Splatting, addressing both 3D foundation models and video generation efficiency.
papers.title: ResStreamGS: Residual-Sensitive Dual-Stream Gaussian Splatting for Mobile Volumetric Video Streaming
papers.tldr: ResStreamGS improves mobile volumetric video streaming by separating temporally stable Gaussians from residual-sensitive ones, reducing payload while enhancing reconstructed quality and maintaining real-time performance.

papers.abstract: We identify a theoretical incompatibility between 3D point cloud masked autoencoding and SE(3)-equivariant networks. We prove that standard masking triggers a topological collapse, effectively forcing the model to hallucinate orientation without a reference frame. To resolve this, we introduce SIEVE (Scalar Invariant Extraction Via Equivariance), an SE(3)-equivariant self-supervised framework that compresses point cloud geometry into invariant scalar embeddings. At its core is the spherical projection mask, which preserves global pose while obfuscating local semantics, sidestepping the obstruction by construction. Experiments confirm that SIEVE circumvents the predicted collapse where constant and noise masks fail. On downstream point cloud tasks, the resulting embeddings improve over coordinate-based baselines and hand-crafted geometric descriptors, with the largest gains on generalization to unseen shape categories.
authors: Jongann Lee, Sun Woo Park, Yun Young Choi
bullets: Standard masking is theoretically incompatible with SE(3)-equivariant networks because it removes the reference needed to infer orientation.
SIEVE extracts geometry into SE(3)-invariant scalar embeddings.
Its spherical projection mask preserves global pose while hiding local semantics.
Experiments show SIEVE avoids the collapse observed with constant and noise masks.
The embeddings outperform coordinate-based and hand-crafted geometric baselines, especially on unseen shape categories.
papers.selection_reason: SE(3)-equivariant self-supervised point-cloud learning with invariant scalar embeddings; relevant to 3D pretraining and geometric representation learning.
papers.title: SIEVE: Overcoming Topological Obstruction in Equivariant Self-Supervised Learning
papers.tldr: SIEVE avoids a topological collapse in equivariant point-cloud masked autoencoding by using pose-preserving spherical projection masks and invariant scalar embeddings.

papers.abstract: Camera-to-robot pose estimation from a monocular image is significant for vision-based robot navigation and control. However, recovering 3D structural features from 2D observations remains a challenging task. Existing camera-to-robot pose estimation methods either rely on time-consuming iterative rendering or involve sophisticated 2D-3D registration which suffers from projection ambiguity, accumulated errors for distal joints and imbalanced learning for different joints. In this work, we propose RoPE-Flow, an end-to-end flow matching-based framework for camera-to-robot pose estimation. From the predicted 2D heatmaps, we propose a Keypoint-centered Feature Extractor to obtain positional features along with contextual representations from keypoints-centered multi-scale patches. Moreover, we introduce Graph-guided Condition Generator, which embeds a learnable adjacency map to generate condition for flow matching based on correlation among keypoints. Besides, we introduce Bone Length Loss and Ray-Depth Loss for topological consistency and scale stability, with joint-wise weighting to mitigate varied prediction difficulty across joints. The proposed method outperforms state-of-the-art methods for pose estimation across different types of robots with mutiple cameras. Besides, we establish a novel cross-scene benchmark to demonstrate the outstanding performance of RoPE-Flow on zero-shot cross-scene robot pose estimation. Meanwhile, animated visualizations are shown on the website: ropeflow.netlify.app
authors: Liangjing Shao, Wanhao Liu, Zhiwei Fang, Rulin Zhou, Quanlu Zhang, Changjing Liu, Beilei Cui, Yiming Huang, Hongliang Ren
bullets: Addresses projection ambiguity, distal-joint error accumulation, and imbalanced joint learning in monocular robot pose estimation.
Extracts positional and contextual features from predicted 2D heatmaps using keypoint-centered multi-scale patches.
Uses a learnable keypoint adjacency graph to condition flow matching on relationships among joints.
Introduces bone-length and ray-depth losses with joint-wise weighting for topological consistency and scale stability.
Reports state-of-the-art performance across robot types and cameras, including zero-shot cross-scene evaluation on a new benchmark.
papers.selection_reason: Monocular camera-to-robot pose estimation via flow matching and graph-conditioned keypoints; relevant to embodied perception and 3D geometry.
papers.title: RoPE-Flow: Monocular Vision-based Robot Pose Estimation via 2D Graph-Conditioned 3D Flow Matching
papers.tldr: RoPE-Flow estimates 3D camera-to-robot poses from a single image using graph-conditioned flow matching and topology-aware losses.

papers.abstract: Spatial agents have access to reconstruction and segmentation tools, yet inconsistent predictions and fragmented object identities can prevent their outputs from becoming reliable 3D scene information. A simple oracle experiment exposes this perception bottleneck: replacing tool-predicted perception with ground-truth 3D bounding boxes raises an agent to nearly full score across five object-centric VSI-Bench tasks, while retaining the same reasoning tools. Motivated by this finding, we believe the devil of spatial reasoning lies in 3D itself, and introduce DeSpatial(Devil of Spatial), which explicitly decomposes spatial understanding into perception and reasoning. DeSpatial has a shared 3D perception tool to reconcile independent perception outputs into a unified, metric, gravity-aligned 3D scene. This perception tool has two core components: a) a joint segmentation--depth co-refinement module that consolidates masks of the same object and removes projection artifacts caused by inconsistent segmentation and depth within a single frame; b) a cross-view instance fusion module that consolidate voxel-overlapping instances but not allowed to merge same-frame instances. This fusion module additionally fuses spatially disjoint fragments caused by insufficient multi-view observations, by checking their 3D structure and source mask appearance. After receiving the complete and unified 3D scene information, the agent chooses reasoning or computational tools to solve the spatial problem. DeSpatial achieves leading performance on VSI-Bench, MindCube-Tiny, and ViewSpatial, with additional long-video results on VSI-SUPER, revealing the bottleneck of spatial understanding lies in a precise 3D perception itself.
authors: Yifei Liu, Xiaolong Zhou, Ziyang Gong, Yifan Zhou, Yuanyuan Gao, Yuning Gong, Yuchen Yang, Hongjie Zhang, Xue Yang, Xiao Sun, Zhihang Zhong
bullets: An oracle experiment finds that ground-truth 3D boxes nearly solve five object-centric VSI-Bench tasks, exposing perception as the main bottleneck.
DeSpatial explicitly separates 3D perception from downstream reasoning and computation.
Its shared perception tool builds a metric, gravity-aligned scene using joint segmentation–depth refinement and cross-view instance fusion.
The system prevents erroneous merges while reconnecting fragmented instances using 3D structure and mask appearance.
It achieves leading performance on VSI-Bench, MindCube-Tiny, and ViewSpatial, with additional long-video evaluation on VSI-SUPER.
papers.selection_reason: Agentic spatial reasoning decomposed into unified 3D perception and reasoning; directly relevant to spatial intelligence and 3D scene understanding.
papers.title: DeSpatial: The devil of Agentic Spatial Reasoning Lies in 3D Itself
papers.tldr: DeSpatial shows that reliable agentic spatial reasoning depends primarily on accurate, unified 3D perception rather than reasoning alone.

papers.abstract: Cultural heritage documentation increasingly relies on image-based 3D surface reconstruction, with photogrammetry software making such workflows accessible to archaeologists, conservators, and heritage technicians. These tools have been successful for conventional multi-view acquisition, but they do not routinely exploit richer multi-view, multi-light data, despite its potential for improving fine-scale surface reconstruction. This limitation is particularly relevant in heritage contexts, where controlled-light acquisition devices such as RTI domes are already used to capture illumination-varying image sets. The challenge is therefore to connect these existing acquisition practices with recent computer vision methods in a form that can be used within operational heritage workflows. In this work, we address this need by integrating state-of-the-art components from computer vision for multi-view, multi-light surface reconstruction into Meshroom, an open-source photogrammetry framework. Rather than proposing a new reconstruction algorithm, our contribution is to assemble and expose existing advanced methods, namely a complete photometric stereo ecosystem (calibrated, self-calibrated and universal), automatic object masking, and multi-view normal-and-reflectance integration, within a usable heritage-oriented workflow. The proposed system thus provides an intermediate software layer between computer vision research code and practical cultural heritage applications, making recent techniques easier to use and evaluate.
bullets: Addresses the limited use of illumination-varying image sets in conventional photogrammetry-based heritage documentation.
Builds on existing tools rather than introducing a new reconstruction algorithm.
Integrates calibrated, self-calibrated, and universal photometric stereo, automatic object masking, and multi-view normal-and-reflectance integration.
Provides a practical software layer connecting computer vision research methods with heritage acquisition practices such as RTI dome imaging.
Supports easier application and evaluation of fine-scale surface reconstruction techniques in operational workflows.
papers.selection_reason: Multi-view multi-light surface reconstruction integrated into photogrammetry workflows; fits 3D vision perception and geometry.
papers.title: Integrating Multi-view Multi-light Surface Reconstruction into Cultural Heritage Workflows
papers.tldr: Integrates advanced multi-view, multi-light reconstruction methods into Meshroom to make them usable in cultural heritage documentation workflows.

papers.abstract: Generating novel views from limited observations requires preserving both the appearance and spatial structure of a scene. Although recent approaches exploit fine-grained geometric cues, they do not explicitly model high-level semantic and spatial properties such as object identity, attributes, and inter-object relationships. In this work, we investigate whether 3D language understanding can provide complementary supervision for novel-view generation. We introduce Ask4NV, built on a pretrained unified multimodal model with a Mixture-of-Transformers (MoT) architecture. Our model incorporates camera geometry into both VAE and ViT representations and leverages understanding features during generation through joint self-attention with a modality-aware attention masking strategy. Experiments demonstrate strong image quality and geometric consistency in novel-view generation, alongside competitive 3D language understanding. Further analysis shows that joint training improves cross-view correspondence in VAE representations and similarity in a 3D-aware feature space.
authors: Jahyeok Koo, Hyeonseo Yu, Seungho Jang, Jaewoo Jung, Jiwon Kang, Seokju Cho, Seungryong Kim
bullets: Targets the challenge of preserving both scene appearance and spatial structure from limited observations.
Introduces Ask4NV, built on a pretrained unified multimodal Mixture-of-Transformers model.
Encodes camera geometry in VAE and ViT representations and integrates understanding features via masked joint self-attention.
Achieves strong image quality and geometric consistency while maintaining competitive 3D language understanding.
Joint training improves cross-view correspondence and 3D-aware feature similarity.
papers.selection_reason: Investigates using 3D language understanding (spatial questions) to supervise novel-view generation. This combines 3D reasoning with generative models, relevant to 3D foundation models and spatial intelligence.
papers.title: Can Learning to Answer Spatial Questions Improve Novel-View Generation?
papers.tldr: Ask4NV uses 3D language understanding and camera-aware multimodal modeling to improve the visual quality and geometric consistency of novel-view generation.

papers.abstract: Feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) methods enable efficient reconstruction of 3D scenes from sparse multi-view images in a single forward pass, without scene-specific optimization. However, existing feed-forward scene-coding pipelines first generate a complete Gaussian representation and then encode its geometry and appearance attributes separately, often involving non-differentiable operations. The resulting 'generate-then-compress' pipeline requires complex attribute-specific codec designs and limits rate-distortion performance by restricting the exploitation of cross-attribute redundancy. We propose multi-view feature coding for Gaussian splatting (MFGS), an end-to-end feed-forward framework for scene coding. Instead of compressing an explicit Gaussian representation, MFGS extracts multi-view features from the input images and encodes them into a compact bitstream. Through end-to-end rate-distortion training, MFGS learns compact multi-view features that jointly represent geometry and appearance, enabling the receiver to predict Gaussian attributes from the decoded features. We further introduce importance-guided Gaussian selection to accommodate different rendering budgets, allowing the receiver to adjust the number of Gaussians used for rendering from the same bitstream. Across RE10K, ACID, and DL3DV, MFGS achieves 99.76-99.86% bitrate savings over the generate-then-compress pipeline, as measured by BD-rate, while reducing total GMACs by 52-55% and providing an approximately 12 times end-to-end speedup.
authors: Seungmi Choi, Ji-Hyoun Choi, Suhyun Jo, Tae-Gwon Park, Hui Yong Kim
bullets: Avoids the conventional generate-then-compress pipeline and its separate, non-differentiable attribute codecs.
Uses end-to-end rate-distortion training to encode multi-view image features into a compact bitstream.
Predicts Gaussian attributes from decoded features while exploiting redundancy between geometry and appearance.
Importance-guided Gaussian selection supports adjustable rendering budgets from a single bitstream.
Across RE10K, ACID, and DL3DV, reports 99.76–99.86% BD-rate savings, 52–55% lower GMACs, and about 12× faster end-to-end processing.
papers.selection_reason: Feed-forward 3D Gaussian splatting scene coding with rate-distortion efficiency.
papers.title: Feed-Forward Multi-View Feature Coding for 3D Gaussian Splatting
papers.tldr: MFGS directly codes compact multi-view features to jointly represent 3D geometry and appearance, enabling faster, more efficient feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting reconstruction.

papers.abstract: Anatomical labels help 3D Gaussian splatting preserve vessels in cinematic renderings of CT, but the representation is still found by optimising each patient's scene, where densification decides where Gaussians go, while real-time displays cap their number. We address one part of this process: deciding where a fixed budget of B Gaussians should be placed. We propose a reusable, labelaware allocation front end that maps a patient's CT, labels and transfer function to a density over 2mm cells and draws exactly B positions from it without per-patient optimisation; the other Gaussian attributes are still fitted per patient. The front end is learned once from per-patient optimised scenes and implemented as a population-trained neural prior and an interpretable seven-parameter visibility-aware closed form (VACF). With identical attribute fitting on 20 held-out patients at 10K-100K Gaussians, both raise vessel-masked PSNR over uniform allocation by 4.5-7.1dB and over pruning a dense voxel-aligned model by 1.6-3.3dB. The neural prior does not differ significantly from per-patient optimised allocation at any budget, and VACF is within 0.6dB of it on vessels; on 19 external patients the neural prior again matches it on vessels and VACF is within 0.7dB. As an initialisation for position optimisation, VACF allocation beats per-patient densification on vessels at 10K Gaussians and, at 25K, reaches a higher vessel PSNR after 118s of optimisation than densification after 248s. Under altered rendering presets, VACF transfers to new colours and lighting but not to a label-free transfer function, whereas the neural prior shows the opposite pattern.
authors: Bowen Xiang, Dingjie Su, Jon S. Heiselman, Michael I. Miga
bullets: Addresses budget-constrained Gaussian placement for cinematic CT rendering, while per-patient fitting still determines other Gaussian attributes.
Maps CT, anatomical labels, and a transfer function to a cell-level density and samples exactly B Gaussian positions.
Introduces a learned neural prior and an interpretable seven-parameter visibility-aware closed form (VACF), trained from optimised scenes.
Across held-out and external patients, both methods outperform uniform and dense-model-pruning allocations; the neural prior matches per-patient optimisation, while VACF remains close.
VACF improves vessel quality and optimisation speed as an initialisation, but transfer depends on the rendering setup and availability of labels.
papers.selection_reason: Addresses budget constraints in 3D Gaussian Splatting for medical imaging by proposing a reusable, label-aware allocation front end and neural prior.
papers.title: Where Should the Gaussians Go? Reusable Label-Aware Allocation for Budget-Constrained Gaussian Splatting of Cinematic CT
papers.tldr: A reusable label-aware Gaussian allocation strategy places a fixed rendering budget where CT vessels matter, improving vessel quality and speeding position optimisation without per-patient allocation search.

papers.abstract: Feed-forward Gaussian reconstruction builds 3D scenes directly from input images for novel view rendering, but learning Gaussian attributes from predicted geometry for high-quality rendering under large viewpoint changes remains challenging. We analyze limitations in Gaussian attribute learning and introduce InfiniSplat v2, which improves rendering quality through architectural and training changes. Our method decouples geometry and attribute prediction with a frozen geometry branch, aligns predicted Gaussians using ground-truth camera poses during training, and adopts large-angle target view supervision. Across six datasets, the feed-forward outputs of the same trained model achieve state-of-the-art mean LPIPS and DISTS among the evaluated methods in both pose-conditioned and pose-free settings. In the pose-conditioned setting, mean LPIPS and DISTS decrease by 25.8% and 32.9%, respectively, compared with the strongest evaluated baselines. We further find that opacity learned with only image reconstruction supervision suppresses geometrically inconsistent points. Project page: https://zju3dv.github.io/InfiniSplat2/
authors: Yongzhen Hu, Hao Yu, Jiawei Wang, Xianming Zeng, Jianyun Xu, Xingliang Liu, Ruizhen Hu, Xiaowei Zhou, Hujun Bao, Sida Peng
bullets: Targets high-quality novel-view rendering from input images, especially under large viewpoint changes.
Decouples geometry and Gaussian-attribute prediction with a frozen geometry branch.
Uses ground-truth camera poses for Gaussian alignment during training and large-angle target-view supervision.
Achieves the best mean LPIPS and DISTS among evaluated methods across six datasets in both pose-conditioned and pose-free settings.
In the pose-conditioned setting, mean LPIPS and DISTS improve by 25.8% and 32.9% versus the strongest evaluated baselines; scope is feed-forward reconstruction under the tested settings.
papers.selection_reason: Improves Feed-Forward 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) by decoupling geometry and attributes, achieving state-of-the-art rendering quality.
papers.title: InfiniSplat v2: Analyzing and Improving Feed-Forward 3DGS from Any Views
papers.tldr: InfiniSplat v2 improves feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting for large viewpoint changes by separating geometry and attribute learning and using stronger view-aware supervision.

papers.abstract: Large view synthesis models (LVSMs) reconstruct scenes from sparse views and render novel views quickly, but they incur unnecessary storage and rendering costs due to token redundancy. We present GLoD-LVSM, a compact, geometry-grounded scene representation for LVSMs with continuous levels of detail. First, instead of learning a fixed set of scene anchor initializations, GLoD-LVSM learns a continuous field that initializes a flexible number of anchors to match the desired budget. A condenser then aggregates scene information into these anchors, with both the field and condenser trained end-to-end. Second, the condenser infers reference-token and anchor geometry to guide compression through geometry-grounded attention, improving rendering quality and enabling frustum culling during decoding. Compared with existing LVSM scene-compression baselines, GLoD-LVSM achieves the best trade-off between rendering quality and scene token count. Compared with the uncompressed base model, GLoD-LVSM reduces the scene-token count by 33.4% and accelerates rendering by $1.23\times$ with no quality loss. Under a relaxed quality-loss budget, the reduction increases to 85.5%, with $3.00\times$ rendering speedup. Further analysis reveals that view-synthesis supervision yields emergent scene depth and self-organized anchors that align with surfaces and adapt their density to local texture complexity. Beyond rendering, we further show that our scene representation also supports scene-semantic understanding, highlighting its potential for broader downstream tasks.
authors: Weikai Lin, Nicholas Milef, Carl S Marshall, Grant Kaijuin Yang, Todd Keeler, Yuhao Zhu
bullets: Addresses token redundancy that increases LVSM storage and rendering costs.
Learns a continuous field to initialize flexible numbers of scene anchors for different token budgets.
Uses an end-to-end condenser with geometry-grounded attention to guide compression and enable frustum culling during decoding.
Reduces scene tokens by 33.4% with no quality loss and provides a 1.23× rendering speedup; under relaxed quality loss, reductions reach 85.5% with 3.00× speedup.
Learned anchors self-organize along surfaces and adapt density to local texture complexity; the representation also supports scene-semantic understanding.
papers.selection_reason: Geometry-grounded continuous-LoD scene representation for large view synthesis models, reducing token count and accelerating rendering.
papers.title: GLoD-LVSM: Learning Geometry-Grounded Continuous-LoD Scene Representations for Large View Synthesis Models
papers.tldr: GLoD-LVSM compresses LVSM scene representations with continuous, geometry-grounded anchors to reduce tokens and accelerate novel-view rendering while preserving quality.

papers.abstract: Human mesh recovery (HMR) provides a geometric foundation for understanding human motion, but accurately reconstructing both body motion and fine hand articulation from videos remains challenging, especially in real-world scenes where occlusion and partial visibility are common. Video generation pretraining offers rich spatial and temporal priors for this task, but its focus on visual synthesis leaves a gap between these representations and explicit human geometry. We present DreamHMR, a general framework that adapts video generation priors for complete body-and-hand reconstruction. It follows a global-to-local strategy, first grounding video representations in human geometry and then refining body and hand detail with reliable local evidence. Global Body Representation Transfer trains the video backbone to predict complete human renderings, turning its native prediction task into a means of learning surface correspondence and posed geometry. Local Joint Feature Enhancement combines contextual estimates with reliable local evidence to recover fine body and hand detail, while limiting interference from occluders and background. Experiments on five datasets with four video backbones demonstrate strong reconstruction performance across backbone families. Under a unified evaluation protocol, our best model outperforms the best existing methods on all reported metrics of 3DPW, EMDB-1, and RICH, reducing body MPJPE by 4.2%, 4.7%, and 6.1%, respectively. In more challenging occlusion settings on held-out BEDLAM and EgoBody sequences, DreamHMR reduces overall body and hand MPJPE by 7.0% and 10.0%, respectively. Our code will be made publicly available.
authors: Zhengjie Xu, Ruihao Gong, Xianglong Liu
bullets: Addresses the gap between video-generation representations and explicit human geometry in human mesh recovery.
Uses a global-to-local design: first learns complete human geometry, then refines body and hand details from reliable local evidence.
Global Body Representation Transfer trains the video backbone to predict complete human renderings and learn surface correspondence.
Local Joint Feature Enhancement combines contextual predictions with local evidence while reducing interference from occluders and background.
Across five datasets and four video backbones, it reports improved body and hand reconstruction performance, especially under occlusion.
papers.selection_reason: Adapts video generation priors for 3D human body and hand mesh recovery, relevant to 3D vision.
papers.title: DreamHMR: From Video Generation to Human Motion Modeling via Structural Focusing
papers.tldr: DreamHMR adapts video-generation priors to recover complete human body and hand motion from videos, improving robustness to occlusion and partial visibility.

papers.abstract: Reconstruction of 3D structures using under-ice AUV video footage has been inaccurate, although it is not certain whether this is due to shortcomings in the methods or an inherent deficiency of the capture system. We test four different models for reconstruction on the same Antarctic under-ice AUV video (Icefin, Kamb Ice Stream): classical feature matching SfM, differentiable photometric splatting, volumetric depth fusion, and a pose-free feed-forward foundation model. All four fail, each in a distinct way: near-total registration yielding almost no structure, geometrically broken output despite healthy photometric metrics, a persistent coverage artifact, and unstable cross-chunk scale. We show that all four are consistent with the same capture regime, a small camera-baseline-to-scene-depth ratio. Following our analysis, we propose a detection system that flags this type of failure in minutes, rather than hours of wasted compute.
authors: Ana-\c{S}tefania Kog\u{a}lniceanu, Kl\'ara Orb\'an, Ashwin Nedungadi, Stefan L\"udtke, Kuderna-Iulian Ben\c{t}a
bullets: Evaluates four reconstruction approaches on the same Antarctic under-ice AUV video.
All methods fail differently: insufficient registration, geometric distortion, coverage artifacts, or unstable scale.
The failures share a common cause: a low camera-baseline-to-scene-depth ratio.
Proposes a detector that flags likely reconstruction failure within minutes instead of after extensive computation.
papers.selection_reason: Analyzes and predicts failure regimes of 3D reconstruction from underwater AUV video, relevant to robust 3D vision.
papers.title: Why 3D Reconstruction Breaks Down on Under-Ice AUV Video, and How to Predict It
papers.tldr: Under-ice AUV video can make 3D reconstruction fail across very different methods because the camera baseline is too small relative to scene depth, but this failure can be detected quickly.

papers.abstract: Recent video world models have increasingly adopted 3D memory mechanisms to integrate historical observations into a lightweight and persistent scene representation. This naturally raises a complementary question: if 3D representations can serve as an effective mechanism for memorizing observed scenes, can they also be directly used as the latent space for reconstructing and generating scenes? Motivated by this idea, we represent a scene as a compact and unstructured 3D-anchored latent space (\textbf{SceneAE}). Each latent combines an explicit 3D position with an implicit content feature and is spatially grounded to describe its local scene region, forming a sparse latent point cloud. Unlike conventional video-VAE latents that describe how a scene appears from particular viewpoints, our representation directly describes the scene itself, making it naturally applicable to both reconstruction and generation. For reconstruction, once the scene has been generated, our persistent 3D representation can be projected and decoded into RGB-D observations by different target cameras, without the need to regenerate a video for each new camera trajectory. For generation, we leverage the geometry-content separation to first generate camera-controlled 3D geometry and then synthesize content conditioned on it, reducing camera-appearance entanglement and improving camera controllability. Experiments show that this 3D latent achieves superior generation quality, computational cost, and camera controllability.
authors: Shuofeng Sun, Wenzhao Zheng, Yunpeng Zhang, Yi Wu, Linqing Zhao, Haibin Yan
bullets: Addresses whether 3D memory representations can serve directly as latent spaces for scene reconstruction and generation.
Represents each scene with spatially grounded 3D positions plus implicit content features, forming a sparse latent point cloud.
Projects the persistent representation into RGB-D views from new cameras without regenerating videos for each trajectory.
Separates geometry generation from content synthesis to reduce camera–appearance entanglement and improve camera control.
Experiments report improved generation quality, computational cost, and camera controllability.
papers.selection_reason: Introduces a 3D-anchored latent space for scene generation and reconstruction, fitting World Models (interactive generation) and 3D Vision.
papers.title: SceneAE: Scene Generation and Reconstruction in Queryable 3D-Anchored Latent Space
papers.tldr: SceneAE represents scenes as sparse, queryable 3D-anchored latents that support both camera-flexible reconstruction and controllable generation.

papers.abstract: Accurate 3D reconstruction in real-world environments remains a significant challenge due to the coexistence of reflective and non-reflective surfaces, which pose distinct modeling demands. Existing methods often treat these surface types separately, limiting their generalizability and physical plausibility. To bridge this gap, we propose MicroSDF, a novel neural implicit framework that facilitates geometry and reflectance modeling through microfacet theory. Our approach incorporates three core innovations: (i) a microfacet-guided geometry model that extracts multi-scale surface normals (macroscopic and microfacet) from a signed distance field (SDF), regularized by a proposed microfacet normal consistency loss to enforce physically plausible surface orientations; (ii) an enhanced dual-branch color model, where the specular branch leverages the microfacet normals to model high-frequency reflectance, and the vanilla branch, unlike prior works, uses reflection direction (instead of viewing direction) to better model diffuse and low-frequency specular components; and (iii) a detection-guided color blending strategy that adaptively fuses the color outputs based on reflection priors, providing more physically intuitive blending than implicitly learned blending weights. Combined with a tailored multi-stage optimization scheme, the proposed MicroSDF achieves robust and high-fidelity reconstruction across reflective and non-reflective surfaces. Extensive experiments on DTU, Shiny Blender, Ref-NeRF, and DeepVoxels datasets demonstrate state-of-the-art performance, establishing a new direction for physically grounded neural reconstruction.
authors: Lejia Ye, Yuhua Xu, Yulan Guo, Lian Xu, Xiaohu Zhang
bullets: Targets the difficulty of modeling mixed-reflectance scenes with a unified neural implicit framework.
Extracts macroscopic and microfacet normals from the SDF and enforces their consistency for physically plausible geometry.
Uses dual color branches: microfacet normals for high-frequency specular effects and reflection direction for diffuse and low-frequency components.
Adaptively blends color predictions using reflection priors rather than implicitly learned weights.
Reports robust, high-fidelity reconstruction and state-of-the-art performance across DTU, Shiny Blender, Ref-NeRF, and DeepVoxels.
papers.selection_reason: Presents a novel neural SDF framework for mixed-reflectance surface reconstruction, contributing to 3D Vision techniques relevant to robotics and simulation.
papers.title: MicroSDF: Microfacet-Driven Hybrid Neural SDFs for Mixed-Reflectance Surface Reconstruction
papers.tldr: MicroSDF reconstructs both reflective and non-reflective surfaces by combining SDF geometry with microfacet-based reflectance modeling and physically guided color blending.

papers.abstract: Single-image 3D reconstruction has advanced rapidly, yet standalone garments remain challenging due to thin-shell geometry, open boundaries, and layered structures. Existing datasets and evaluation protocols provide limited support for systematic evaluation in this setting. We introduce MagicGarment, a benchmark for single-image standalone 3D garment reconstruction with 1,518 professionally constructed assets across 17 composite garment types, aligned multimodal annotations, and a unified evaluation protocol. We further establish a garment-aware reference baseline by adapting a pretrained image-to-3D backbone at two levels: Grounded Semantic Refinement (GSR) provides garment-focused visual conditioning, while Flow-Time-Route LoRA (FTR-LoRA) adapts the frozen 3D generative backbone using flow-timestep, token-routing, and expert-load information. Experiments demonstrate MagicGarment's benchmark utility and the effectiveness of garment-aware adaptation. Project page: https://1019538157.github.io/MagicGarment/.
authors: Jia Chen, Ruyang Zhao, Jun Bai, Chao Huang, Saishang Zhong, Xinrong Hu
bullets: Addresses challenges from thin-shell geometry, open boundaries, and layered garment structures.
Provides 1,518 professionally constructed assets spanning 17 composite garment types.
Includes aligned multimodal annotations and a unified evaluation protocol.
Adapts a pretrained image-to-3D model with garment-focused visual conditioning and flow-aware LoRA refinement.
Experiments show the benchmark is useful and the garment-aware adaptation is effective.
papers.selection_reason: Introduces a benchmark and adaptation method for single-image 3D garment reconstruction using a pretrained backbone, fitting 3D Vision and 3D Foundation Models.
papers.title: MagicGarment: Benchmarking Single-Image Standalone 3D Garment Reconstruction
papers.tldr: MagicGarment introduces a benchmark and garment-aware baseline for evaluating single-image 3D reconstruction of standalone garments.

papers.abstract: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) enables high-quality, real-time novel view synthesis but requires significant storage and transmission resources. Mapping Gaussian attributes to 2D representations enables efficient compression using mature image codecs. However, Gaussian representations that achieve comparable rendering quality are generally treated similarly during optimization, despite substantial differences in coding rate, leading to limited rate-distortion (R-D) performance after compression. To address this limitation, we propose RDCompGS, a 3DGS compression method that enables overall R-D optimization of Gaussian representations with respect to subsequent coding. A differentiable estimate of the coding rate is incorporated into the R-D optimization with rendering distortion. The rate constraint adjustment model further regulates the R-D trade-off across different compression conditions. Extensive experiments on three benchmark datasets demonstrate that RDCompGS achieves average Bj{\o}ntegaard Delta Rate reductions of 37.84% and 49.31% with H.265/HEVC and JPEG XL, respectively. The estimated rate also shows a strong correlation with the actual bit-rate under different compression conditions.
authors: Huiping Ren, Shuai Wan, Luqian Bai, Zhang Chen, Fuzheng Yang
bullets: Targets the high storage and transmission cost of 3DGS while preserving novel-view rendering quality.
Maps Gaussian attributes to 2D representations and incorporates differentiable coding-rate estimates into rate-distortion optimization.
Uses a rate-constraint adjustment model to control the trade-off across compression conditions.
Across three benchmark datasets, reduces average BD-Rate by 37.84% with H.265/HEVC and 49.31% with JPEG XL.
Estimated rates strongly correlate with actual bitrates under varying compression conditions.
papers.selection_reason: 3D Gaussian Splatting compression with rate-distortion optimization; fits 3D scene representation.
papers.title: RDCompGS: Rate-Distortion Optimization for Compression of 3D Gaussian Splatting with Image Codecs
papers.tldr: RDCompGS improves 3D Gaussian Splatting compression by jointly optimizing rendering quality and estimated image-codec bitrate.

papers.abstract: As a lightweight and highly accurate method for nearest-neighbor search in 3D point clouds, approaches based on space-filling curves (SFC) have been proposed. However, due to the inherent properties of SFC, a gap arises between proximity relationships along the SFC and those in the original Euclidean space. In this study, we propose a loss function that reduces the influence of this gap. Specifically, we compute the distances between adjacent points along the SFC and train the model to optimize feature similarity between pairs of points that are distant from each other in the original 3D space. We incorporate the proposed method into a high-performing 3D point cloud segmentation model and evaluate its effectiveness on three datasets. The results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms conventional methods on both indoor and outdoor point cloud datasets.
authors: Konan Sasaki, Junya Komori, Kazuhiro Hotta
bullets: SFC-based neighbor search is efficient but can connect points that are far apart in 3D space.
The method computes distances between adjacent points along the SFC.
It trains feature similarity for point pairs that are distant in Euclidean space but close along the SFC.
The loss is integrated into a high-performing 3D point-cloud segmentation model.
Evaluation on three datasets shows improvement over conventional methods in both indoor and outdoor settings.
papers.selection_reason: 3D point cloud segmentation with space-filling-curve neighbor gap loss; fits 3D vision perception.
papers.title: Reducing the Gap Between Spatial and Space-Filling Curve Neighbors in 3D Point Cloud Segmentation
papers.tldr: A novel loss reduces the mismatch between space-filling-curve and Euclidean neighbors, improving 3D point-cloud segmentation across indoor and outdoor datasets.

papers.abstract: We present LidarVerse, a real-time unified LiDAR world model for sensor simulation across tasks and sensors. Existing LiDAR simulators largely follow one of two complementary paradigms: reconstruction-based methods preserve the geometry of a captured scene but require lengthy per-scene optimization, whereas generative methods amortize learning across data but lack the consistency needed for long-horizon rollouts. LidarVerse brings both paradigms into a single, unified conditional generative framework. A universal tokenizer maps LiDAR range sequences into a shared latent space, where a bidirectional teacher learns a common interface for conditioning on a LiDAR prefix, an HD-Map, a persistent spatial cache, and optionally, text. Varying the available scene evidence turns the same model into a generator of new worlds, a point-cloud forecaster, or a generalizable resimulator of observed scenes without per-scene optimization. We distill the teacher into a four-step autoregressive causal student and maintain both a rolling temporal K/V cache and a world-aligned spatial cache, enabling persistent long-horizon rollouts with real-time inference at 11 FPS on a single H100 GPU. LidarVerse achieves state-of-the-art performance on most reported metrics across all three evaluation protocols, while its tokenizer supports 32-, 64-, and 128-beam LiDAR and generalizes to an unseen scanning pattern. These results demonstrate that generative and reconstruction-grounded LiDAR simulation can be realized within one model, providing the core capabilities for future closed-loop sensor simulation.
authors: Henry Che, Xuanchi Ren, Sanja Fidler, Shenlong Wang, Laura Leal-Taix\'e, Shengyu Huang
bullets: Combines reconstruction-based scene consistency with the scalability of generative modeling in one conditional framework.
Uses a universal tokenizer and a shared latent interface conditioned on LiDAR prefixes, HD maps, spatial memory, and optionally text.
A single model supports new-world generation, point-cloud forecasting, and resimulation without per-scene optimization.
A distilled four-step causal student with temporal and spatial caches enables persistent long-horizon rollouts at 11 FPS on one H100 GPU.
Reports state-of-the-art performance on most metrics across three evaluation protocols and generalizes across LiDAR beam counts and an unseen scanning pattern.
papers.selection_reason: Unified LiDAR world model for sensor simulation and forecasting, fitting world models and 3D perception.
papers.title: Into the LidarVerse: A Real-Time Unified LiDAR World Model Across Tasks and Sensors
papers.tldr: LidarVerse is a unified, real-time LiDAR world model that supports world generation, forecasting, and scene resimulation across sensors and tasks.

papers.abstract: As the Arctic transitions toward a seasonally ice-free state, capturing the complex morphology of submerged sea ice is crucial for advancing models of ocean-ice-atmosphere heat exchange and monitoring under-ice habitats. Currently, sub-surface ice mapping is predominantly achieved through acoustic sensors such as multibeam sonar. While sonar provides robust large-scale geometry, it lacks spectral and high-resolution textural information required to record fine morphological features - a critical limitation in under-ice environments, where sparse visual features and degraded sensing conditions challenge the capture of detailed structural and optical surface properties. We present a benchmark for vision-based under-ice 3D reconstruction using real-world data from the MOSAiC expedition and synthetic data generated in an Unreal Engine-based underwater robotics simulator. The benchmark evaluates Structure-From-Motion (SfM) and monocular depth estimation, with quantitative comparison enabled through cross-modal registration to upward-looking multibeam sonar.
authors: Kl\'ara Orb\'an, Ashwin Nedungadi, Ana-\c{S}tefania Kog\u{a}lniceanu, Bianca-Marcela Sava, Bastian Cieply, Raul-Alexandru Simon, Kuderna-Iulian Ben\c{t}a, Stefan L\"udtke
bullets: Addresses the limited textural and spectral detail provided by sonar for fine-scale submerged sea-ice morphology.
Uses real-world MOSAiC expedition data alongside synthetic imagery from an Unreal Engine underwater robotics simulator.
Evaluates Structure-From-Motion and monocular depth estimation methods.
Enables quantitative assessment through cross-modal registration with upward-looking multibeam sonar.
Targets challenging conditions including sparse visual features and degraded underwater sensing.
papers.selection_reason: Benchmark for under-ice 3D reconstruction and monocular depth estimation; fits 3D vision.
papers.title: Benchmarking 3D Reconstruction for Under-Ice Robotic Perception in Arctic Environments
papers.tldr: A benchmark evaluates vision-based 3D reconstruction for detailed under-ice mapping using real and synthetic Arctic data, with sonar-based geometric comparison.

papers.abstract: Monocular 3D object detection methods increasingly rely on depth-guided transformers, but they operate entirely in the perspective image plane where spatial relationships are distorted by foreshortening. We propose MonoMIP, a dual-decoder framework that adds complementary 3D geometric reasoning through Bird's-Eye View (BEV) features constructed via Multi-Height Inverse Perspective Mapping. We perform IPM at K elevation planes spanning ground to rooftop, producing an ordered stack of height-conditioned metric BEV features that reduces above-ground misprojection and exposes depth-dependent appearance variation across planes. A BEV decoder with multi-scale deformable attention aggregates this multi-height evidence per query, while a depth-guided 3D decoder provides complementary perspective-space predictions. Without extra training data, MonoMIP attains 25.84% Moderate AP3D|R40 on KITTI val and 21.66% on the official test set for Car, outperforming recent published monocular methods on both the KITTI and Waymo benchmarks.
bullets: Addresses perspective distortion and above-ground misprojection in monocular 3D detection.
Constructs ordered metric BEV features using inverse perspective mapping across K elevation planes from ground to rooftop.
Uses a deformable-attention BEV decoder alongside a complementary depth-guided 3D decoder.
Reports 25.84% Moderate AP3D|R40 on KITTI validation and 21.66% on the official test set for cars.
Evaluated on KITTI and Waymo without extra training data; scope is monocular 3D object detection.
papers.selection_reason: Monocular 3D object detection with BEV geometric reasoning, fitting 3D perception.
papers.title: MonoMIP: Multi-Height Inverse Perspective Mapping for Monocular 3D Object Detection
papers.tldr: MonoMIP improves monocular 3D detection by combining multi-height BEV geometric reasoning with depth-guided perspective decoding.

papers.abstract: Real measurements are too limited to train an accurate indoor pathloss predictor that works across a wide range of buildings. Large-scale synthetic pretraining offers a way forward, but real building layouts are also scarce, and accurate ray-tracing simulators are slow, expensive, and often proprietary. We address both problems by introducing a generator that automatically creates diverse indoor layouts and a fast, open-source approximate ray tracer that computes radio maps for them. Using this pipeline, we generate 128M synthetic samples, pretrain ResNet-101 and Swin-T encoder-decoders, and fine-tune them on high-quality benchmark data. Despite simulator mismatch, our ResNet-101 model reduces error by 15% on average relative to the best known methods across five indoor radio-map prediction tasks and improves transfer on a small real-measurement dataset. Both architectures show predictable data-scaling trends: power laws fitted on 2M-16M samples predict the mean normalized downstream RMSE at 32M-128M with 3.33% mean absolute percentage error for ResNet-101 and 7.10% for Swin-T. These results show that pretraining on large amounts of cheap simulated data can improve indoor radio-map prediction, even when real measurements and high-quality simulations are limited.
authors: Khoren Petrosyan, Artashes Mkrtchyan, Rafayel Mkrtchyan, Hrant Khachatrian, Theofanis P. Raptis
bullets: Addresses scarce real measurements, building layouts, and costly proprietary ray tracing.
Introduces an automatic indoor-layout generator and a fast open-source approximate ray tracer.
Pretrains ResNet-101 and Swin-T encoder-decoders on 128M synthetic samples, then fine-tunes on benchmark data.
ResNet-101 reduces error by 15% on average across five tasks and improves transfer to a small real-measurement dataset.
Scaling trends follow predictable power laws, with downstream RMSE forecasts remaining reasonably accurate at larger data scales.
papers.selection_reason: Uses synthetic 3D indoor layouts and ray tracing to pretrain models for radio-map prediction, demonstrating a transferable pipeline for 3D spatial understanding and foundation model pretraining.
papers.title: Scaling Cheap Synthetic Pretraining Improves Indoor Radio-Map Prediction
papers.tldr: Large-scale pretraining on cheaply generated synthetic indoor radio maps substantially improves prediction despite imperfect simulation fidelity.

papers.abstract: Sparse-to-dense motion completion recovers dense mesh motion from sparse vertex displacements. Residual priors trained on one geometry family frequently fail to beat parameter-free harmonic extension off-family. Moreover, cross-family training meets a scaling barrier: residual amplitude varies by more than an order of magnitude across geometry families and collapses as observations become denser. Since this scale depends on unknown target motion, it cannot be measured directly at test time. We decouple residual structure from physical scale by learning a dimensionless prior, estimating amplitude from observables and a lightweight correction fitted only on training sources. Our unified model surpasses harmonic extension across all evaluated families, including unseen cloth and legged bodies, without skeletons, registration, or cross-mesh correspondence. The same prior applies without retraining to point-tracked animal video and a robot grasping a soft body. Project page: https://su-terry.github.io/cepheid-website/
bullets: Addresses the failure of geometry-specific residual priors and cross-family scaling differences.
Learns a dimensionless motion prior, then estimates scale from observations with a lightweight training-source correction.
Works without skeletons, registration, or cross-mesh correspondence.
Outperforms harmonic extension across evaluated families, including unseen cloth and legged bodies.
Transfers without retraining to point-tracked animal video and robot–soft-body grasping.
papers.selection_reason: Presents a cross-family 3D motion completion method with a scale-invariant prior, relevant to 3D geometry and transferable to embodied and soft-body settings.
papers.title: Cepheid: Decoupling Scale from Structure for Cross-Family Motion Completion
papers.tldr: Cepheid enables cross-family sparse-to-dense motion completion by separating residual motion structure from its unknown physical scale.

papers.abstract: 3D part assembly aims to reconstruct a complete shape from a set of unassembled parts by predicting a rigid SE(3) transformation for each part. Because the placement of a part is rarely determined by its own geometry, the task demands reasoning over the entire part set, and existing methods, which rely on pairwise relations or iterative generation and verification, scale poorly to objects with many parts. We present LLM2R, which casts part assembly as sequence modeling with a pretrained decoder-only large language model (LLM): a Point-BERT encoder and a Q-Former compress each part into a block of geometric tokens, the blocks of all parts are concatenated, and a causal LLM adapted with Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) processes the sequence in one forward pass. Causal attention, however, lets the hidden states of a part observe only the parts that precede it. LLM2R therefore appends a block of learnable summary tokens after the last part: these tokens follow every part, so their states aggregate the whole assembly at a constant token cost, and a part-aware pose head fuses each part's states with them before predicting its rotation and translation. One architecture thus handles semantic and geometric assembly and predicts all poses in a single non-autoregressive pass. LLM2R achieves the highest part accuracy and success rate on all three PartNet categories, the best rotation error, translation error, and part accuracy on PartNeXt, and the lowest translation error and fastest inference on Breaking Bad, where only a fracture-specialized method is more accurate. Its advantage grows with the number of parts: at 100 parts it exceeds GARF by 33.5 points in part accuracy on Breaking Bad and Assembler by 29.1 points on PartNet, and it transfers zero-shot to unseen categories with more than 16 points higher part accuracy than the strongest of three baselines.
authors: Zhouhan Zhong, Qiuhong Shen, Xingyi Yang, Jinyi Xu, Xinchao Wang
bullets: Problem: Pairwise and iterative assembly methods struggle as the number of parts grows because placement depends on the full set.
Method: Point-BERT and a Q-Former encode each part into geometric-token blocks, which a LoRA-adapted causal LLM processes in one pass.
Key design: Learnable summary tokens aggregate information from all parts and are fused with each part’s states to predict rotation and translation.
Results: LLM2R achieves leading or competitive accuracy, pose errors, success rate, and inference speed across PartNet, PartNeXt, and Breaking Bad.
Scope: It transfers zero-shot to unseen categories and its advantage increases for assemblies with many parts.
papers.selection_reason: LLM-based 3D part assembly with geometric token sequence modeling; relevant to 3D foundation models and spatial reasoning.
papers.title: LLM2R: From Large Language Models to 3D Reassemblers
papers.tldr: LLM2R reframes 3D part assembly as one-pass sequence modeling with an LLM, enabling scalable prediction of all part poses using global assembly context.

papers.abstract: Parametric Computer-Aided-Design (CAD) modeling from human intent remains challenging, particularly during the conceptual design stage, where design goals are expressed through incomplete and unstructured modalities (e.g., hand-drawn sketches and textual descriptions). In this work, we rethink the human intent-to-CAD pipeline and propose a unified method that directly maps multi-level human intents to executable codes, without assuming the prior existence of target CAD models. To support our study, we construct HiCAD, the first large-scale dataset aligning hand-drawn sketches, textual descriptions, and parametric CAD codes. Based on this, we introduce HiCAD, a two-stage framework comprising Cooperative Multi-Task Alignment to bridge the representational gap between heterogeneous inputs, and Spatial-Aware Reinforcement Learning to enforce geometric and topological consistency. Extensive experiments demonstrate that our method significantly outperforms existing baselines across multiple tasks, validating its effectiveness and robustness in transforming heterogeneous human intents into high-fidelity parametric CAD models. Our project page: https://zqwlearning.github.io/HiCAD.
authors: Qingwang Zhang, Jiahao Li, Xiangdong Zhou
bullets: Addresses conceptual CAD design from incomplete, heterogeneous human intents without requiring pre-existing target CAD models.
Introduces a dataset aligning hand-drawn sketches, textual descriptions, and parametric CAD codes.
Uses Cooperative Multi-Task Alignment to bridge representations across input modalities.
Applies Spatial-Aware Reinforcement Learning to promote geometric and topological consistency.
Reports improved performance and robustness over existing baselines across multiple tasks.
papers.selection_reason: Parametric CAD model generation from sketches and text is 3D geometry generation, fitting 3D Vision.
papers.title: Rethinking Human Intent-to-CAD: Parametric CAD Model Generation via Cooperative Multi-Task Alignment and Spatial-Aware Reinforcement Learning
papers.tldr: HiCAD directly transforms sketches and text into executable, high-fidelity parametric CAD models by combining multi-task alignment with spatially aware reinforcement learning.

papers.abstract: Implicit neural representations (INRs) are shaped by the spectral structure induced by their input encodings and activation functions. Existing methods improve fitting primarily by modifying which frequencies are available to the network, through coordinate encodings or periodic nonlinearities. However, frequency access is not the only bottleneck: signals with localized or spatially varying structure require the network to efficiently compose frequencies into multi-harmonic internal responses. We introduce learnable spectral activations (LSA), which replace fixed neuron-level nonlinearities with a residual truncated Fourier series whose harmonic amplitudes are learned during training. LSA does not expand the asymptotic function class. Instead, it changes the factorization of the representation: linear weights select features while activation coefficients control spectral shaping, and the two are updated by separate gradients. Because the activation output is affine in the coefficients given fixed pre-activations, spectral tuning becomes a more direct subproblem compared to architectures where it is entangled with feature selection. Empirically, this factorization concentrates more target-signal energy in the leading eigenmodes of the neural tangent kernel, consistent with improved optimization behavior. Across audio, image, neural radiance field, and neural acoustic field tasks, LSA also improves reconstruction quality.
bullets: Problem: Existing encodings and periodic activations expand frequency access but may struggle with localized or spatially varying structures requiring multi-harmonic composition.
Method: Replace fixed activations with residual truncated Fourier series whose harmonic amplitudes are learned during training.
Key idea: Linear weights select features while activation coefficients independently control spectral shaping, without expanding the asymptotic function class.

Result: The factorization concentrates more target-signal energy in leading neural tangent kernel eigenmodes and improves reconstruction quality across audio, image, neural radiance field, and neural acoustic field tasks.
papers.selection_reason: Introduces learnable spectral activations for implicit neural representations, relevant to 3D vision and efficient representation learning.
papers.title: Learnable Spectral Activations
papers.tldr: Learnable Spectral Activations improve implicit neural representations by learning how neurons compose frequencies, enabling better optimization and reconstruction across several signal domains.

papers.abstract: LLM-based agents are increasingly capable of generating complex 3D structures, with the potential to reshape how objects are designed and realized in the physical world. Yet, producing elegant geometry is fundamentally different from producing objects that can be built and perform their intended functions. Existing evaluations largely focus on geometric quality while overlooking physical realizability. We introduce LMBuild, a benchmark for evaluating LLM agents on generating buildable and functional structures. LMBuild represents generated objects as assembled structures comprising part decompositions, joints, materials, and sequences. To support reproducible evaluation, we provide a unified framework consisting of: (1) an interactive environment in which agents can use tools to retrieve, create, and place components to construct objects; (2) a curated benchmark that repurposes established CAD datasets and augments them with knowledge from Wikipedia; and (3) a evaluation framework covering structural soundness, functional affordance, design quality, and physical realization. Evaluations across 30 systems reveal several intriguing findings: (a) Soundness and alignment are no longer the primary bottlenecks for frontier closed-source models, while functional affordance and physical operability remain substantially more challenging; (b) stronger models more effectively create new components, whereas weaker models tend to rely on retrieval; and (c) providing functional specifications substantially improves part completeness, kinematics, and physical operability. These results show that generating real-world structures requires deeper reasoning about functional affordances, mechanics, and designing and creating novel components. We expect LMBuild to provide a foundation for measuring progress and incentivizing research toward agents that generate buildable and functional structures.
bullets: Evaluates assembled structures defined by parts, joints, materials, and construction sequences.
Provides an interactive tool-use environment, a CAD- and Wikipedia-enhanced benchmark, and metrics for soundness, function, design quality, and physical realization.
Across 30 systems, functional affordance and physical operability remain harder than structural soundness and alignment for frontier closed-source models.
Stronger models create novel components more effectively, while weaker models rely more on retrieving existing components.
Functional specifications improve part completeness, kinematics, and physical operability.
papers.selection_reason: Introduces a benchmark for LLM agents generating 3D structures, relevant to 3D vision and foundation models.
papers.title: LMBuild: Evaluating LLM Agents for Generating Buildable and Functional Structures
papers.tldr: LMBuild benchmarks LLM agents on generating 3D structures that are not only geometrically sound but also buildable and functionally operable.

papers.abstract: Reconstructing complete, high-quality meshes of large-scale scenes from unposed multi-view images requires faithful geometric grounding while plausibly completing surfaces that are unobserved or only sparsely captured. We present WorldRecon, a generative multi-view reconstruction framework for recovering complete, large-scale 3D scene meshes from unposed RGB images. WorldRecon uses a coarse, noisy global point cloud and camera poses estimated from the input images by a reconstruction model as a global scaffold for whole-scene generation and partitions it into overlapping spatial blocks. To robustly leverage these imperfect geometric priors, we equip the native 3D generative model TRELLIS.2 with a dedicated reconstruction-based conditioning architecture that generates each block from its local point-cloud crop and block-relevant image observations, producing sparse structure, detailed geometry, and PBR materials. To maintain scene-level coherence, we introduce neighbour-aware latent inpainting and a causal world-generation procedure that propagates structural, geometric, and material context across overlapping blocks. Together, these designs scale multi-view generative reconstruction to large-scale scenes, yielding coherent, unified meshes. Extensive experiments demonstrate that WorldRecon achieves state-of-the-art reconstruction performance, reducing Chamfer distance by 14.9% and 43.1% while improving F-score by 17.3% and 12.0% over the strongest baselines on synthetic and real-world indoor scenes, respectively, thereby demonstrating faithful and complete generative reconstruction as well as strong sim-to-real generalization. Project page: https://kszpxxzmc.github.io/WorldRecon-website/.
authors: Mengchen Zhang, Yang Li, Chunshi Wang, Tong Wu, Chunchao Guo
bullets: Addresses incomplete or sparsely observed surfaces and imperfect camera/geometry estimates in large-scene reconstruction.
Uses a coarse global point cloud and estimated poses as a scaffold, partitioning scenes into overlapping spatial blocks.
Conditions TRELLIS.2 on local point-cloud crops and relevant images to generate structure, detailed geometry, and PBR materials.
Employs neighbour-aware latent inpainting and causal generation to maintain coherence across overlapping blocks.
Reports improved reconstruction on synthetic and real-world indoor scenes, including lower Chamfer distance and higher F-score than baselines.
papers.selection_reason: Generative multi-view mesh reconstruction for large-scale 3D scenes, directly relevant to 3D vision and scene generation.
papers.title: WorldRecon: Generative Multi-View Mesh Reconstruction for Large-Scale 3D World
papers.tldr: WorldRecon generates coherent, complete large-scale 3D meshes from unposed multi-view RGB images by combining noisy global geometry with block-wise generative reconstruction.

papers.abstract: Reliable robot autonomy requires reasoning about the world from partial and noisy observations. However, many perception systems model only visible scene regions, rely on fixed semantic categories, and assume reliable sensor measurements. These assumptions break under occlusion, novel object encounters, and sensor degradation. In this paper, I present a research vision for incompleteness-aware scene understanding. I organize this vision around three fundamental challenges: incomplete evidence, incomplete knowledge, and incomplete sensor reliability. I discuss my research contributions toward addressing these challenges through amodal perception, semantic occupancy forecasting, open-world scene understanding, label-efficient learning, and uncertainty-guided multi-modal fusion. Building on these contributions, I outline future research directions toward belief-centric 4D scene representations. These representations aim to jointly model geometry, semantics, motion, and uncertainty. I also discuss active sensing and safe adaptation strategies that allow robots to reduce uncertainty through interaction. The goal is to develop calibrated and actionable scene representations that support reliable autonomy in dynamic, open-world environments.
bullets: Identifies three challenges: incomplete observations, incomplete semantic knowledge, and uncertain sensor reliability.
Proposes addressing them with amodal perception, semantic occupancy forecasting, open-world understanding, label-efficient learning, and uncertainty-guided multimodal fusion.
Envisions belief-centric 4D scene representations combining geometry, semantics, motion, and uncertainty.
Highlights active sensing and safe adaptation as ways for robots to reduce uncertainty through interaction.
Focuses on calibrated, actionable representations rather than assuming complete visibility or fixed categories.
papers.selection_reason: Incompleteness-aware spatial scene understanding and belief-centric 4D representations for robot autonomy, relevant to embodied AI, spatial intelligence, world models, and 3D vision.
papers.title: Perception Beyond the Visible: Incompleteness-Aware Scene Understanding for Robot Autonomy
papers.tldr: A research vision for robot perception that explicitly models missing evidence, unknown objects, and unreliable sensors to enable safer autonomy in dynamic open-world environments.

papers.abstract: We present CoTL, a framework that learns a compact set of tokens that preserves scene geometry and appearance from unposed multi-view images. Our encoder compresses the input images into small per-view sets of latent tokens that aggregate information across views to form a view-consistent scene representation. Each additional view expands the representation with only a small, resolution-independent set of tokens, allowing its capacity to grow with the available observations. To force this compact bottleneck to retain sufficient scene information, a query-based Gaussian decoder uses scene-independent queries to attend to the learned tokens and recover an explicit, renderable set of 3D Gaussian primitives. Novel-view rendering supervision trains the compact representation end to end through the reconstructed Gaussian scene. Experiments on \retenk{} and ACID show that the resulting compact, unstructured token set supports competitive novel-view synthesis and can serve as the latent space of a generative model for 3D Gaussian scene generation. Together, these results show that 3D Gaussian reconstruction is an effective objective for compact scene representation learning and the learned token space provides a basis for broader downstream tasks in 3D vision.
authors: Han Liang, Sibo Wu, Anpei Chen, R\"udiger Westermann
bullets: Compresses each input view into a small, resolution-independent set of latent tokens.
Aggregates tokens across views so representation capacity grows gradually with additional observations.
Uses scene-independent queries in a Gaussian decoder to reconstruct explicit 3D Gaussian primitives.
Trains end to end with novel-view rendering supervision through the reconstructed scene.
Demonstrates competitive novel-view synthesis on RĕNTeK and ACID, with tokens also usable for generative 3D Gaussian modeling.
papers.selection_reason: Compact token learning for 3D scene representation and novel-view synthesis, fits 3D vision.
papers.title: CoTL: Compact Token Learning for 3D Scene Representation
papers.tldr: CoTL learns a compact, view-consistent token representation from unposed multi-view images and decodes it into renderable 3D Gaussian scenes for competitive novel-view synthesis.

papers.abstract: We present a real-time, hybrid framework for occlusion handling and depth-aware tracking in minimally invasive surgeries (MIS). Occlusions caused by surgical instruments often obscure the region of interest (ROI), affecting surgical precision. To address this, our approach integrates enhanced You Only Look Once (YOLO) based detection, Particle Filtering (PF), and monocular depth estimation using Multiple Depth Estimation Accuracy with Single Network (MiDaS). Occlusion is detected using a distance-based threshold between instruments and ROI. Experimental results demonstrate robust instrument detection with a confidence score of 0.85, effective occlusion event handling, and accurate depth prediction with an MAE of 0.34 cm and RMSE of 0.53 cm. Independent phantom-based validation against stereo depth measurements yielded an MAE of 0.65 cm and RMSE of 0.66 cm. The framework further achieved an occlusion detection accuracy of 81.95\% while maintaining real-time performance at 38.7 FPS. Preliminary surgeon feedback indicates that the proposed visualization framework is clinically relevant and holds promise for future intraoperative image-guided navigation and decision support in MIS.
authors: Anuska Sarkar, Partha Acharya, Vishnu Nandury, Kaustav Basu, Subhamoy Mandal
bullets: Targets loss of ROI visibility caused by surgical instruments during minimally invasive surgery.
Uses enhanced YOLO for instrument detection, particle filtering for tracking, and MiDaS for monocular depth estimation.
Detects occlusions through a distance-based threshold between instruments and the ROI.
Achieves 81.95% occlusion detection accuracy at 38.7 FPS, with reported depth errors varying across evaluation settings.
Phantom validation and preliminary surgeon feedback support potential use in intraoperative navigation and decision support.
papers.selection_reason: Depth-aware occlusion handling and monocular depth estimation for surgical visualization, relevant to 3D perception.
papers.title: Augmenting Real-time Visualization in Minimally Invasive Surgery with Particle Filtering and Depth-Aware Occlusion Handling
papers.tldr: A real-time MIS visualization framework combines enhanced YOLO, particle filtering, and monocular depth estimation to detect and manage instrument-induced occlusions while tracking depth.

papers.abstract: End-to-end deep learning pipelines for camera-radar 3D object detection are well established in driver assistance systems and autonomous vehicles; however, adapting them to roadside-mounted infrastructure presents significant challenges. On vehicles, sensor heights, pitch angles, and relative geometries remain largely uniform, allowing end-to-end models to generalize effectively. On the contrary, roadside sensor installations vary drastically in height, tilt, and field of view across locations, rendering end-to-end models prone to failure and difficult to adapt without massive location-specific datasets. Hence, instead of designing a complex end-to-end pipeline for direct 3D bounding box estimation, a low-cost, resource-efficient two-stage approach is proposed for real-time 3D shape and orientation estimation. The first stage utilizes any off-the-shelf, state-of-the-art method to extract 2D camera bounding boxes and associated 3D radar points for each road user. The proposed second stage then processes these inputs to construct 3D oriented bounding boxes where radar data determines 3D position, predefined templates define size for each road user, and a tiny neural network predicts a site-specific and optimized yaw angle. The algorithm is successfully validated at a curved road with a junction for pedestrians, bicycles, and cars, where it achieves 25 frames per second on an NVIDIA Jetson ORIN for real-time applications.
authors: Shiva Agrawal, Savankumar Bhanderi, Gordon Elger
bullets: Addresses the poor portability of end-to-end camera-radar 3D detection models across roadside locations with differing sensor geometries.
Uses off-the-shelf 2D camera boxes and associated 3D radar points as inputs to a lightweight second stage.
Estimates 3D position from radar, object dimensions from predefined road-user templates, and yaw from a small neural network.
Validated on pedestrians, bicycles, and cars at a curved road junction, running at 25 frames per second on an NVIDIA Jetson ORIN.
Scope: the yaw model is site-specific, so adaptation across locations remains necessary.
papers.selection_reason: Proposes a resource-efficient two-stage approach for 3D shape and orientation estimation using camera and radar data, fitting the 3D Vision category.
papers.title: Resource-Efficient 3D Shape and Orientation Estimation of Road Users using Roadside RGB Camera and 3D Radar
papers.tldr: A resource-efficient two-stage system combines camera detections, 3D radar, templates, and a tiny site-specific network to estimate oriented 3D boxes for road users in real time from variable roadside installations.

papers.abstract: RGB-based category-level 9D pose estimation remains highly challenging because a monocular system must generalize across unseen object instances while jointly inferring 3D translation, 3D rotation, and 3D size. Unlike instance-level pose estimation, the category-level setting requires the network to learn both what is shared across objects within a category and how individual instances vary in structure.
